爽了，Codex 现在也能直接做广告大片了！！！

我给 Codex 装上 PixVerse 的插件，用它的 Skill 一键做出了一支 40 秒的滑雪镜广告（我们自己家销量最好的滑雪镜哦）：悬崖后空翻、雪粉扑满镜头、云海日落，最后落在产品特写和 logo 上，配乐卡点，还有英文旁白。

从分镜图到视频、配乐、配音，全部是 AI 生成的，没有一帧实拍😅

我来给大家详细讲一讲怎么做的：

1、丢产品图：我只给了三张雪镜的产品图，一句话说清楚要一支"高级感的滑雪运动广告"。

2、Codex 先出分镜图：很多人不知道，Codex 本身就能出图。它拿着这三张产品图，一口气出了 40 多张分镜图：镜片微距、雪墙急转、起跳、空中最高点、落地、云海背影……每一张里的雪镜都是同一副，黑框、红金镜片、皮标、蓝色纹样绑带等，都非常完美展示。

3、定节奏：冷开场，起跳那一下音乐炸开，空中后空翻，最后落在产品特写上。我就讲了这么一段话。

4、挑镜头：每个镜头它都会出两个版本，我只负责挑动作最干净、产品最清楚的那条。

分镜图出好以后，PixVerse 的 Skill 接着干了这些：

1、图生视频加首尾帧：用 PixVerse 自家的 V6 把分镜图变成镜头，给起跳和最高点两张图，它就能把中间的空翻补出来。

2、配乐：一句情绪描述就出整首配乐，冷开场、起跳炸开、结尾终击都有。

3、配音：旁白直接挑 ElevenLabs、MiniMax 的预设人声，我选了一个成熟的美式男声，开场三个词 "Breathe. Focus. Commit."，结尾一句 "Bollfo. See further."

4、按节拍剪：起跳、落地、换场都卡在重拍上，最后统一响度直接出片。

积分情况：1080P 视频大概 16 积分一秒，一条 5 秒的镜头 80 积分，一首配乐 50 积分，旁白 50 个字才 1 积分。每批生成之前它都会先报价，生成完逐条记账。

最离谱的是，这个插件里有 30 多个现成的 Skill，产品广告、带货短片、开箱、短剧都有。模型除了 PixVerse 自家的 V6，还能直接切 Seedance 2.5、可灵、Veo等

最后给一个小提示：Codex 干活很猛，但审美真的不太够😅 它能把镜头做出来，却看不出哪条别扭、哪里变形。

我的做法是先让 Claude 当审美总监，看动作自然不自然、产品有没有走样、剪点有没有卡在拍上，再由 Claude 指挥 Codex 去出图、调 PixVerse 生成。一个负责看，一个负责做，出来的效果好太多了。

做品牌广告、电商短片，或者要给客户出片的朋友，强烈建议去试一下！

text:
according to my recent analysis of ~30k Trust Wallet addresses trading perps on Hyperliquid, users lost money mainly to liquidations and fees. 

tools that help users lose less already exist, but eventually how to fit them into a smooth mobile app comes down to product taste.

one way is to show the market. hyperdash's liquidation heatmap shows where liquidations are stacked: if a large block of long liquidations sits at one price, touching it fires a wave of market sells, pushes price lower and sets off the next layer. traders can see where a cascade might start. it's a good tool, but making it easy to read on a phone is where product taste comes in.

another way is to show your own position. so, non-pro traders (like me) also need to know how big a move our own account can take before it gets liquidated.

phantom's new perps screen brings this to a much wider group of users. As you change leverage, it shows how your size, liquidation price and potential profit move, with tp/sl on the same screen. It shows users what they're doing and what they're risking, and makes it easy to control that risk before a fomo trade.

text:
The paradox of fast learning:

The faster you learn, the slower you perceive your progress.

Ever since we launched the RareSkills ZK Tutor for AI, I noticed an increase in students who were *dissatisfied* with the rate of their progress *despite* the fact that they *measurably* mastered material 4-6x as fast as students in the traditional "classroom" setting we occasionally do.

Here's my hypothesis:

If you learn a new field extremely fast, you race past the first peak of the Dunning-Kruger curve so quickly you enter the "trough of despair" almost immediately.

The more you learn about a field, the more you realize you don't know! So the faster you learn about a new field, the more you become aware of your ignorance.

I don't have a solution to this, because this seems to be a general human condition. Every person with a modicum of wisdom has said some version of "the more I know, the more I realize the less I know."

My suspicion is that the correct perspective is not trying to measure your own knowledge, but rather whether your "learning lifestyle" is one to be proud of.

Regardless of how much or how little you know, do you feel the need to keep learning and act on it as a habit?

If you look back and see you've used your time wisely, you should feel proud of yourself. Don't try to evaluate how much you know relative to the field.

text:
Don’t count on a V-shaped recovery this time.

2020’s Covid crash was saved by the Fed and vaccines. 2025’s Tariff selloff  had the tariff pause. Both selloffs had catalysts, and ultimately, headlines that helped the market recover.

This time around the Fed is hiking, the 10Y is above 5%, the AI trade is unwinding, and the market’s biggest leader has lost $2.5T in market cap. 

What headline fixes all that?

When liquidity tightens and market leadership breaks down, bottoms tend to be built, not snapped back into. That takes time, consolidation, and new leaders emerging.

Not saying the market has to crash or that a V-shaped recovery is impossible. But I think patience matters more than buying every dip. Keep scanning for stocks making higher lows and showing relative strength. That’s where the next leg higher will likely begin.

text:
Commodities are getting hit pretty hard alongside the broader equity market as the surging U.S. dollar sucks liquidity out of the global financial system.  For those that follow me, I've been saying this from some time that there was risks if the dollar strengthens too quickly. 

The issue is that dollar-denominated debt becomes more expensive to service, financial conditions tighten, and investors are forced to raise cash, reduce leverage and sell assets. It becomes less about fundamentals and more about liquidity.

One thing I've learned over the years is that market leverage doesn't necessarily tell you when a correction will happen, but it tells you a great deal about how painful that correction could become. For some perspective, U.S. margin debt has surged to approximately $1.45 trillion, equivalent to roughly 58% of U.S. currency in circulation and 6.2% of M2 money supply. That's an extraordinary amount of leverage in the system, and when markets start moving against investors, it can accelerate the selling pressure.

Unfortunately, even gold isn't immune. During a liquidity-driven selloff, investors often sell what they can, not necessarily what they want to. Gold can become a source of cash to cover margin calls and offset losses elsewhere.

The irony is that the very forces driving the dollar higher could eventually create the conditions for its reversal. The U.S. government and broader financial system have become increasingly reliant on negative real interest rates to help manage an enormous debt burden. A prolonged dollar-driven liquidity squeeze makes that increasingly difficult, raising the risk that something eventually breaks and forces central banks to step in with lower rates and additional liquidity.

That's when things can get interesting for gold. It may get sold during the initial panic, but if policymakers respond by driving real interest rates back into negative territory, the combination of easier money and renewed currency debasement concerns could send gold sharply higher. 

In other words, the same liquidity squeeze hurting gold today could ultimately create the conditions for its next rally. 

We're watching  all of this closely and remaining deliberate about managing exposure through what continues to be a challenging market environment through to the end of the year.

BREAKING: This past week's -10.4% drop in the Nasdaq 100 was one of the rarest weekly declines in 40 years.

Of the last 2,133 trading weeks, just 11 saw declines of this magnitude or worse.

That's 0.52% of all weeks, a 3.27 standard deviation move based on the historical mean and volatility.

Of course, market returns exhibit "fat tails," meaning extreme moves occur more frequently than a normal distribution would predict.

However, even accounting for the fact that extreme market moves are more common than traditional statistical models suggest, this was a historically rare selloff.

Volatility returns when markets least expect it.

author: SemiAnalysis_

text:
Using our AgentX dataset as a rough estimate of the token mix corresponding to $44k in output, we arrive at an estimate of $125k all in.

It's impossible to say what the shape of this workload actually was. Alpöge describes working on this proof over the course of several weeks, so it's possible that the final proof was a small fraction of the total cost. 

On the other hand, in SemiAnalysis’s internal usage, we observe that human-in-the-loop work doesn't burn many tokens compared to asynchronous agentic work, which is what produced the proof. It’s therefore also possible that the two proof artifacts represent most of the total cost. (3/4)

text:
Today’s claim on the Riemann Hypothesis helps demonstrate what I mean when I speak about Computational Reenchantment.

If the proof holds, we’ll likely simplify its explanation to some extent.

But as it stands, it’s 250,000+ pages.

Long enough to indicate that “pages” is a vestige of a mode of formal comprehension we’re rapidly leaving behind.

So really no one, including the proof’s human “author”, comprehends the nature of the proof at full resolution.

But because computational verification scales far more steeply than human comprehension, and because it can offer certain functional guarantees, we will use abstractions we comprehend less and less to do more and more.

At some point this process will produce physical creations indistinguishable from magic and the paranormal, even to their creators.

As we push into the deepest realms of analytic formalism, the phenomenological bottom drops out, leaving us once again grasping for understanding amidst an age of generally inexplicable Angels and Demons.

quoted_text:
The Riemann Hypothesis has fallen.  RH was the singular math result that had been named, in advance, as the obvious coal mine canary for dangerously advanced AI, over the last three decades.  The methods used should generalize to "make AI very good at anything you can definitely test", and unfortunately that category includes "make AI better at making AI".

This is like a private company announcing they have produced a million tons of 15% enriched uranium.  It's not 90% enriched weapons-grade uranium, so you could proclaim the company's output is not immediately deadly right now.  The concern is that the process line may generalize, to an extinction-level threat, within the unpredictably immediate future.  Forecasters still had Riemann at 2035 one week earlier.

This is distinct from earlier events in that earlier you could reasonably ask if AI was selectively picking off famous math problems that turned out to be easier for AI.  The Riemann Hypothesis was the single challenge most often named in advance as a warning sign.

text:
Over the past couple weeks we've met with management teams across memory, optics, neoclouds, semis, semi cap equipment and substrates.

Everyone is frustrated and confused about their stock prices but everyone is still very, very bullish.

Everyone expects 2027 capex to be significantly higher than 2026 and they expect 2028 capex to be moderately to significantly higher than 2027. 

Everyone knows the YoY capex growth rates will decelerate but the total dollars spent will continue to get bigger... at least for the next few years. Everyone says we're still in the early innings of ai adoption. 

Every company in the ai ecosystem is 50-100% sold out for 2027 and 40-80% sold out for 2028. 

Everyone is sitting on LTAs from the hyperscalers... some of those LTAs are getting signed and they last anywhere from 3 years to 6+ years... and they're getting done at record prices and record margins. Customers can't take the chance of not having enough supply to meet their needs over the next 3-5 years... locking up supply at record prices is better than not having enough supply when it's needed the most. 

Some of these LTAs could consume more than 50% of their supply over the next 2-3 years and at least one company has an LTA that would consume 75% of their capacity over the next 2-3 years. 

Neoclouds continue to see demand that is 5-10x higher than capacity. Many of them are saying the financing concerns are overblown. They're seeing 3-5 year deals get signed at 10-20% higher prices that the first half of 2026 and they think deals signed in the first half of 2027 will have 10-20% higher prices than deals signed in the second half of 2026. Power is still a big bottleneck and many sites are dealing with small construction delays but nothing is getting canceled. Customers are desperate for compute. Many of the neoclouds are trying to reserve 10-15% of capacity for shorter term deals and spot market because rates are 2-3x higher than the 3-5 year deals. 

Memory companies say demand will outstrip supply until 2029 at the earliest. They are very confident LTAs won't get cancelled because even at record prices for memory, the customers have enough margin to make it work. 

I know there's lots of fear and uncertainty in the market right now but it's not showing up in the demand... it remains stronger than ever... many backlogs are growing faster than current revenues.

In 20+ years of investing, I've honestly never seen this much dislocation between fundamentals and valuations. This is truly a historic time to be an investor and not in a good way. It's very hard to be patient and lean into your conviction/thesis during times like this but that's probably the right strategy for most long-term investors. 

Hopefully the lows are near. Make sure you are getting sleep, sunlight and exercise. Protect your mental health if possible.

Today we're launching the Data Marketplace for Agents: 100+ providers that agents and developers can find and pay for per call.

Google organized the world's public information, and agents now search it faster than any person could. But a lot of the valuable data isn't on the open web. Data on people, companies, jobs, finance and real estate is kept by data companies, and agents can't easily reach it.

Most of it is still sold by subscription. That works for a product that calls one source thousands of times. An agent needs a little data from a lot of places, and it shouldn't have to buy three subscriptions to make two requests.

Last November, @berasogut1  and I started @orthogonal_sh  to make APIs discoverable and payable by agents. Agents mostly came to us for data, and soon data providers were asking to list with us. So we became a marketplace.

Providers list once, and agents find what they need and pay per call from one balance, over MCP, CLI or API. About 90% of our usage already comes from customers using five or more providers, including @DustHQ, @ZenskarHQ and @foundeers.

text:
You are living through one of the rarest statistical events in modern financial history.

Today, the VIX hit 32.

Most retail investors see a 30+ VIX and panic. But if you study market history and derivatives research, a VIX crossing 30 is one of the rarest and most critical macro signals in finance

In normal markets, the VIX lives between 15 and 20. A VIX  above 30 only happens in about 5% of all trading sessions in history. 

• 1997: Asian Financial Crisis 
• 1998: Russian Default & LTCM Collapse 
• 2000–2001: Dot-Com Bust 
• 2002: Enron & WorldCom Scandals 
• 2008: Great Financial Crisis 
• 2011: U.S. Credit Rating Downgrade 
• 2020: COVID-19 Global Shock 
• April 2025: Tariff & Trade War Repricing 
• March 2026: Geopolitical Escalation

What do all of these have in common? Forced margin liquidations and structural repricing.

But don't mistake extreme fear for an immediate green light.

A 30+ VIX can mark a generational bottom (like 1997, 2011, or 2020) or it can be a devastating bull trap if credit and fundamentals are broken (like 2000 and 2008).
author: 0xDamien
quoted_text:
The five conditions that have called every major bottom of the QE era (outside systemic breaks):

1. VIX above 30
2. Fed not signaling hikes
3. Margin debt deleveraging
4. A clear leading sector
5. That sector beating earnings during the panic

April 2025 hit all five and produced 75%+ inside a year. March 2026 also hit all five and is already up roughly 20% on Mag7 and nearly 40% on semis in a month.

Both times the leading sector was semis and AI infrastructure.

text:
Maybe, but I'd like to offer a counterpoint to this: The new Reimann proof is more similar to an iPhone than it is to a magical, enchanted artifact that defies human explanation. 

What I mean is, no one person understands all the things of how an iPhone works, but many people understand many parts of it so that as a civilization we sort of collectively grasp it in some very vague (and honestly not very useful) sense.

This will happen with these proofs. They will come to us as from a factory in Shenzhen, where (like the iPhone) we don't have the full picture of how each one works, but we can apprehend enough to determine their usefulness to us.

At some point, mathematicians and others will, collectively, have a vague grasp on these proofs the way humans have a vague, collective grasp on the iPhone's workings, and that will be enough and it won't be very weird. We'll get used to this state of affairs pretty rapidly.

i’m trying really hard to be excited about these (objectively awesome) scientific breakthroughs, but there’s something about all of this that just doesn’t sit quite right

i think it’s the fact that these discoveries are being made using models that the rest of us plebs aren’t even allowed to know the names of

models distilled from generations of our collective knowledge, creativity, research, and expertise, whose most powerful capabilities are now being kept behind closed doors

like, just imagine how many brilliant, creative people out there could be making discoveries of their own right now if they simply had access

i want to celebrate these breakthroughs, i really do

but the rebel in me is viscerally enraged at the prospect of a Silicon Aristocracy consolidating control over the means of scientific discovery

that ain’t it, chief

text:
We're in some pretty rough market conditions right now.

As a result, several major chain tokens have dropped in price.

I checked @Alchemy's latest Chain Rankings data to analyze how chain usage impacts its coin price.

Here's a quick breakdown ↓

1. Biggest gainers

→ @Enter_Elysium (+258%)

Elysium (Hyperliquid L2 by @Kinetiq_xyz) launched its mainnet on Nov 9, with Uniswap available from day one.

By Nov 11, Uniswap had already recorded $200M in cumulative trading volume on the network.

That launch-week trading activity likely contributed to the massive increase in usage.

→ @Base (+19%)

Base's Denim upgrade made block production 10x faster, increasing demand for blockchain data.

Trading picked up too, as @aeroxyz Slipstream alone saw a 42.5% increase in weekly volume, while unique active addresses grew by 28%.

So there was actual onchain growth alongside the additional infrastructure activity.

→ @BNBCHAIN (+9.8%)

Trading activity seems to explain much of the increase here.

PancakeSwap V3 and Infinity alone added nearly $1B in weekly DEX volume, which points to a significant increase in trading activity.

2. Biggest losers

→ @monad (−7.5%)

DEX trading volume dropped 5.1% over the week, from $259.6M to $246.4M, which could partly explain the decline in usage.

Interestingly, Monad still recorded a daily transaction record of 10.44M on Nov 13, so the slowdown wasn't happening across the entire network.

→ @0xPolygon (−7%)

Polymarket International's trading volume fell 23.6% in the week following the US midterms.

Looks like the post-election cooldown took a toll on Polygon's activity too.

→ @RobinhoodCrypto (−5.7%)

Active wallets: +30.6%
Transactions: −7.4%
Network fees: −25.8%

Daily active addresses nearly doubled the following day after @metricxyz launched a points program (Nov 12), which explains the growth in active wallets.

I'd say that this decline in txns and network fees is due to the wider market conditions.

3. Usage vs. price

This is probably the most intriguing finding:

• BNB Chain: Usage +9.8% | $BNB −12.8%
• Solana: Usage +2.5% | $SOL −15.9%
• Arbitrum: Usage +3.8% | $ARB −18.8%

Arbitrum also saw 15.6% more DEX trading volume, despite having 7.3% fewer active wallets.

I wouldn't automatically read that increase as bullish. Activity such as people selling, closing positions, or rotating into stablecoins also generates trading volume.

4. My Take

I think we're seeing a liquidity problem more than a network activity problem.

With less liquidity available, selling pressure can move token prices much more aggressively, even while onchain applications remain busy.

That's why @Alchemy's Chain Rankings are so useful alongside price charts. They help distinguish a market that's repricing risk from networks that are actually losing activity.

And judging by this week's data, those are two very different things.

author: servasyy_ai
quoted_text:
爽了，Codex 现在也能直接做广告大片了！！！

我给 Codex 装上 PixVerse 的插件，用它的 Skill 一键做出了一支 40 秒的滑雪镜广告（我们自己家销量最好的滑雪镜哦）：悬崖后空翻、雪粉扑满镜头、云海日落，最后落在产品特写和 logo 上，配乐卡点，还有英文旁白。

从分镜图到视频、配乐、配音，全部是 AI 生成的，没有一帧实拍😅

我来给大家详细讲一讲怎么做的：

1、丢产品图：我只给了三张雪镜的产品图，一句话说清楚要一支"高级感的滑雪运动广告"。

2、Codex 先出分镜图：很多人不知道，Codex 本身就能出图。它拿着这三张产品图，一口气出了 40 多张分镜图：镜片微距、雪墙急转、起跳、空中最高点、落地、云海背影……每一张里的雪镜都是同一副，黑框、红金镜片、皮标、蓝色纹样绑带等，都非常完美展示。

3、定节奏：冷开场，起跳那一下音乐炸开，空中后空翻，最后落在产品特写上。我就讲了这么一段话。

4、挑镜头：每个镜头它都会出两个版本，我只负责挑动作最干净、产品最清楚的那条。

分镜图出好以后，PixVerse 的 Skill 接着干了这些：

1、图生视频加首尾帧：用 PixVerse 自家的 V6 把分镜图变成镜头，给起跳和最高点两张图，它就能把中间的空翻补出来。

2、配乐：一句情绪描述就出整首配乐，冷开场、起跳炸开、结尾终击都有。

3、配音：旁白直接挑 ElevenLabs、MiniMax 的预设人声，我选了一个成熟的美式男声，开场三个词 "Breathe. Focus. Commit."，结尾一句 "Bollfo. See further."

4、按节拍剪：起跳、落地、换场都卡在重拍上，最后统一响度直接出片。

积分情况：1080P 视频大概 16 积分一秒，一条 5 秒的镜头 80 积分，一首配乐 50 积分，旁白 50 个字才 1 积分。每批生成之前它都会先报价，生成完逐条记账。

最离谱的是，这个插件里有 30 多个现成的 Skill，产品广告、带货短片、开箱、短剧都有。模型除了 PixVerse 自家的 V6，还能直接切 Seedance 2.5、可灵、Veo等

最后给一个小提示：Codex 干活很猛，但审美真的不太够😅 它能把镜头做出来，却看不出哪条别扭、哪里变形。

我的做法是先让 Claude 当审美总监，看动作自然不自然、产品有没有走样、剪点有没有卡在拍上，再由 Claude 指挥 Codex 去出图、调 PixVerse 生成。一个负责看，一个负责做，出来的效果好太多了。

做品牌广告、电商短片，或者要给客户出片的朋友，强烈建议去试一下！

成片放在下面了，记得开声音👇

目前我依然傻傻地重仓各种资产，回撤非常痛苦，但我不怪任何人，也不怪自己。我缺的就是这种归零的心态。AI 的冲击肯定有先有后，只是来得比我想象的快。很多聪明人恐怕早就在卖出手上的资产了，他们看到的东西，我们可能还没看到。

这一个月发生的事，单独看都只是新闻，放在一起看就是一条线。
10 月底，OpenAI 和 Anthropic 先后宣布，AI 推翻了「指数时间假设」。这个假设是 1999 年提出的，可以看作 P≠NP 下面的一道防线。它被推翻，不等于 P=NP，但一直押 P≠NP 的计算机科学家 Scott Aaronson 也说，他心里 P=NP 的概率从 3% 调到了 5%。
11 月 20 日，Anthropic 的数学家 Levent Alpöge 宣布，他和 Claude 证明了黎曼猜想。这道题是黎曼在 1859 年提出的，人类追了一百六十多年。证明超过二十五万页，人已经读不完了，只能交给 Lean 这样的程序一步一步检查。目前程序已经跑通，数学界还在做最后的核对。
同一个月，币安被盗约 64 亿美元，是史上最大的加密盗窃案，初步说法是一名运维工程师的笔记本被攻破。接着黄仁勋辞职，英伟达股价大跌。
把这几件事放在一起看，就很魔幻：机器在攻克人类最难的数学题，人却在最简单的地方出错。一边是一百六十多年没人解开的猜想，一边是一台没管好的笔记本。AI 往上走得越快，人在系统里就越像最薄的那一环。

我们正在走向一条越来越混乱的世界线，很多过去被当成理所当然的前提，正在一个个松动。世界线本来是物理学里的概念，指一个物体在时空里走过的轨迹。看过《命运石之门》的人都知道，世界线平时会自己收束，小事改变不了大方向。可是一旦经过某个节点，原本收束的线就会开始分岔，每一个小变量都会被放大。1972 年，气象学家洛伦茨问过一个问题：巴西的一只蝴蝶扇动翅膀，会不会在德州引发一场龙卷风？他的答案是，在混沌的系统里，长期预测本身就做不到。

我觉得我们正在经过这样一个节点。
黑天鹅不再是几十年一遇，而是一个月来好几只。蝴蝶效应也不再只是比喻，一个工程师的笔记本就是那只蝴蝶。
世界线正在从收束走向发散，这个世界会越来越难预测。这种时候，比预测更重要的，是不管走出来的是哪条线，自己都还站得住。

再说比特币。
比特币不是 AI 发明的，它来自 2008 年一份人类写的白皮书。它对 AGI 的意义大不大？
我的想法是，比特币不是国家的替代品，但它可能是第一种不需要人也能持有的钱。未来发生的事情预测不到。换句话说，金融领域的替代品还没降临。现在能够预想到的还远远不够，AI agent 开不了银行账户，却可以拥有一个钱包。Stripe 收购稳定币公司 Bridge，Coinbase 推出给 AI 付款用的 x402 协议，都是在给「非人类」修一条付钱的路。

所以我们需要重新思考 AI 解构一切的顺序。
最早被解构的是金融，因为钱本来就是信息。然后是公司治理，因为公司说到底是一堆合同加上一群人。最晚的是国家治理，因为国家除了信息和合同，还有土地、军队和认同，这三样东西没办法被一行代码改写。到了国家这一层，目前还没有替代品，比特币不算，AI 也还没有发明出来。

我问 Claude Code，现在给我最大的建议是什么。它说：如果让我指一条路，我会拿手上每一样资产去问一个问题，它会被 AI 最先解构，还是最后解构？
越靠近纯信息的东西，越先被冲击，比如靠信息差赚钱的生意、靠一个人撑起来的估值，代码也不例外，比特币说到底也是一串代码。
越靠近物理世界和人心的东西，越晚被冲击，比如电力、土地、算力背后的能源，还有一群人之间真实的信任。这不是叫大家去买什么，而是在重仓之前，先想清楚自己押的是解构的前段，还是后段。

我打算先回归研究一些先哲的智慧，融入之后再去金融市场厮杀。庄子说：「虚室生白。」屋子空出来，光才照得进来。归零不是认输，是把位置腾出来，等新的东西长出来。

text:
14 岁少年采访狱中 SBF：当年为什么只投 Anthropic 5 亿美元？FTX 崩盘到底值不值得？

最近，一名 14 岁少年对正在服刑的 FTX 创始人 SBF 进行了一场长达 80 分钟的采访，聊到了 Anthropic、AI 毁灭人类的风险，以及 FTX 崩盘。

其中几个回答相当值得关注：

- 关于 Anthropic： SBF 表示，当时 Anthropic 只需要约 5 亿美元购买算力，因此只进行了这一规模的融资，而 FTX 几乎包下了整轮融资。

- 关于 AI： SBF 认为，AI 最终导致人类灭绝的概率约为 25%。

- 关于 FTX： 当被问及 FTX 曾经创造的价值是否足以抵消崩盘造成的损害时，SBF 回答「不」。但他补充道：「如果我最后没有搞砸，本来会值得。」

采访最后，SBF 还给这名 14 岁少年提出了人生建议。

从曾经掌管数百亿美元的加密帝国，到如今只能通过监狱电话接受采访，SBF 的处境已经彻底改变。

最让人感慨的是，当年 FTX 投资的 Anthropic 如今已经上市，而 SBF 仍身陷囹圄。

周末研读好文，市场没有信心崩塌，还是正常回调，美国不会傻到把AI掐死，让竞争对手超越。

文章结论：这不是AI泡沫破裂，而是一次正常修正。市场已把大量悲观因素定价进去，高质量科技股风险回报正在变好，情绪极端后买盘会重新回来。保持客观、看数据和人性即可。

过去45天市场经历多重冲击：约6万亿美元市值蒸发、Big Tech资本开支暴增引发自由现金流担忧、中期选举后“特朗普看跌期权”结束、美联储持续加息、英伟达争议叠加Anthropic大规模IPO抽走流动性。科技股远期估值大幅压缩，英伟达已到约9倍，市场几乎不相信其盈利指引。

但基本面并未崩：Q3企业盈利仍强劲增长，AI基建资本开支虽短期压制现金流，却是这场技术革命的必要投入。监管担忧被放大了——美国全面禁止AI的概率极低，否则会把优势拱手让给中国。极端恐慌和资金流出往往出现在修正尾声，一旦流动性恢复，高质量资产更容易被重新定价。

现在不是恐慌的时候，而是重新审视仓位、等待更好风险回报的时候。

SCP-2026应存放于Site-19的标准异常物品储藏室，置于不透明密封容器内。未经3级以上权限批准，禁止对SCP-2026进行直接视觉观察。所有观察必须通过间接摄像设备进行，且单次观察时间不得超过30秒。任何观察到SCP-2026的人员在结束后必须接受心理评估。若发现人员出现持续鼓掌倾向，立即隔离并按标准认知危害协议处理。

Description:
SCP-2026是一张数码照片，拍摄于2026年11月19日纳斯达克交易所某公司上市开盘仪式现场。照片中可见多名个体（包括两名主要人物及周围数人）正双手鼓掌。
SCP-2026的异常性质在于：照片中的所有个体在拍摄瞬间被锁定于“鼓掌”这一动作中，无法停止。无论从何种角度观察，这些个体均持续进行鼓掌动作，频率约为每分钟120-140次。照片本身为静态图像，但通过任何方式观察时，鼓掌动作会以实时方式呈现。

被困个体在异常发生后的数小时至数日内会逐渐表现出明显的生理衰弱迹象：肌肉痉挛、关节肿胀、皮肤磨损、脱水与极度疲劳。最终，所有个体均因持续鼓掌导致的身体衰竭而死亡。死亡后，鼓掌动作仍会继续，直至尸体完全腐坏无法维持动作结构为止。整个过程在照片中可被观察者完整目睹。
目前尚未确认SCP-2026是如何将特定个体困入照片的。已知所有被困个体均为当时现场实际在场人员。照片之外的任何复制品（包括数字拷贝、打印件）均不具备异常性质。

Addendum 2026-1 - 观察记录节选：

观察开始后约4小时：主要男性个体面部出现明显痛苦表情，手臂颤抖，但鼓掌频率未降低。

观察开始后约18小时：一名女性个体因双手持续摩擦导致皮肤大面积撕裂，血液沿手臂流下，鼓掌动作仍在继续。

观察开始后约36小时：全部个体已无生命体征，但身体仍在机械性重复鼓掌动作，直至肌肉完全坏死。

Addendum 2026-2：
曾尝试以其他手段中断鼓掌动作（包括对原照片进行物理破坏、覆盖、销毁尝试），均失败。照片被销毁后会在72小时内于同一位置重新出现，内容完全相同。目前认为该异常具有自我修复特性，且与“仪式性集体鼓掌”这一行为存在关联。
注： 基金会尚未找到解除被困个体状态的方法。所有尝试均以失败告终。

text:
卧槽，OpenAI 联合创始人 Andrej Karpathy 刚刚直接把屏幕分享出来，毫无保留地演示了自己每天是怎么跟大模型打交道的。

整整 70 分钟，没有花里胡哨的 PPT，也没有空洞的理论吹水，全是最顶级的 1% 玩家在真实工作流里和大模型死磕的实操现场。

他拆解出来的核心链路极其克制，就四步：提示词（Prompts）→ 上下文（Context）→ 工具（Tools）→ 工作流（Workflows）——这就是头部玩家每天的真实样子。

说实话，绝大多数人用 AI 之所以卡壳，根本不是模型不够强，而是自己把事情想得太复杂了。Karpathy 的做法其实特别干净利落：挑对模型、喂准上下文、剩下的交给工具去跑。

谁都能打开 ChatGPT 敲几行字聊天，但真正能像这位 OpenAI 联合创始人那样把大模型拧出生产力的，在全网都凤毛麟角。

这一套实操的含金量，恐怕比市面上那些卖两千美金的所谓“AI 进阶课”还要实在得多。

这就好比同样是一把削铁如泥的宝刀，普通人拿在手里只会比划着削铅笔，还嫌刀刃太重；真正的高手却只挑最顺手的角度、递上最对路的材料，借着刀锋的惯性一气呵成。

今天先赶紧把这条视频码住看完，再顺着下面的指南去搞明白，怎么用 Harness、Loops 和 Graphs 把这套日常打法，进一步升级成能自己跑起来的智能体系统。 https://t.co/47AYOLqNc8

text:
越跌反而越兴奋，好像已经觉得不疼了。这次8万多上了仓位被骗的很惨。

倘若市场再次出现2008年金融危机那样的史诗级暴跌，或许就是一次能够让资产翻十倍、实现阶层跃升的巨大机会。
 
2008年我刚工作两年，省吃俭用攒下12万人民币，在年底巴菲特出手之后抄底了巨涛海洋石油，盛高置地等几只港股。那个时候什么都不懂，稀里糊涂。现在回头看，那时候遍地都是十倍股，真的随便买都是十倍，甚至不少百倍股。
 
巴菲特大概在2008年11月左侧抄底，买早了。到年底全球一片萧条，奥巴马上台为市场打气，那年元旦，市场氛围凄风惨雨。等到第二年春天行情大幅反弹，也正是巴菲特说出“如果你等知更鸟报春，春天就要结束了”的时候，短短四五个月，我的资产翻了将近10倍，稀里糊涂赚到了人生第一个a7到100万。
 
一晃将近二十年，股市里面，我再也没有遇到过这种可以随便买都能让资产十倍增长的机会。巴菲特也已经苦苦等了四五年了，一直在等待这样的时机。
 
现在纳斯达克从27700跌到22500，跌幅20%，第一波大跌快要收尾，我预判还会有一次急跌插针，最近一两周全球市场大概率迎来力度较强的第二浪反弹（包括创业版，恒生科技，比特币等等）。但如果AI泡沫真正破灭见底，下跌周期会很漫长，大概率要等到明年年底。
 
美股五浪下跌、五浪上涨的规律向来有参考性，倘若AI泡沫破裂，目前仅仅是第一浪下跌，苹果40倍的市盈率还没有开始消化，本轮下跌主要集中在半导体、英伟达以及存储板块。
 
耐心等待明年底的重大机会，拿住还剩余的子弹，一定要在巴菲特出手之后再出手。

quoted_text:
14 岁少年采访狱中 SBF：当年为什么只投 Anthropic 5 亿美元？FTX 崩盘到底值不值得？

最近，一名 14 岁少年对正在服刑的 FTX 创始人 SBF 进行了一场长达 80 分钟的采访，聊到了 Anthropic、AI 毁灭人类的风险，以及 FTX 崩盘。

其中几个回答相当值得关注：

- 关于 Anthropic： SBF 表示，当时 Anthropic 只需要约 5 亿美元购买算力，因此只进行了这一规模的融资，而 FTX 几乎包下了整轮融资。

- 关于 AI： SBF 认为，AI 最终导致人类灭绝的概率约为 25%。

- 关于 FTX： 当被问及 FTX 曾经创造的价值是否足以抵消崩盘造成的损害时，SBF 回答「不」。但他补充道：「如果我最后没有搞砸，本来会值得。」

采访最后，SBF 还给这名 14 岁少年提出了人生建议。

从曾经掌管数百亿美元的加密帝国，到如今只能通过监狱电话接受采访，SBF 的处境已经彻底改变。

最让人感慨的是，当年 FTX 投资的 Anthropic 如今已经上市，而 SBF 仍身陷囹圄。

text:
孙宇晨最新深度采访完整版：看空BTC，看空纳指，观望ETH，看好AI应用，不玩A股... 严肃分享了很多市场观点和交易仓位，值得一看

看空BTC。认为比特币面对AI和量子计算的威胁很难全身而退，市场低估了这类风险对 BTC 的潜在冲击。抗量子升级只能救"愿意自救的人"，硬分叉冻结老币在比特币的去中心化下几乎不可能达成共识。但是他的BTC是底仓，在过去一年的下跌中并没有减仓。

ETH目前仅2成仓位观望。 在去年 3600–4000 减了八九成的ETH（去年 11–12 月，减持逻辑是 4800 那个"只靠 Tom Lee 续命"的二顶），截至目前仍然没有买回。ETH减仓期间，他增配了美股。

纳指中线"微微看空"，看空但还没做空。认为资金抱团太严重，硬件股被炒成软件股，AI 循环融资一出事全出事。美债是所有资金的"母级"，现在被权益"子级"吸血，利率必须高才接得到钱，高到一定程度钱又会倒流。芯片短期不排除过剩，像 2000 年的光纤。

AI板块最看好应用。尤其 AI 健康管理（数据采集→挖掘→决策，不用等生病才去医院）。最不看好存储、光模块。一个锚：单一企业市值上限≈美债的一半，所以英伟达顶多再翻 4 倍，而应用层能翻 4 倍以上的机会太多了。明年后年主题会分化。

人民币会走强，美债危机被过度担忧。只要美国还握着 AI（芯片、存储、模型）的终极控制权，美债就不缺买家，"孙悟空跳不出如来佛的手掌心"。

基本没有A股仓位，但会做一些研究。对于A股光模块行情，他的解释是，这一方向能够连接美国AI投资需求，同时中国企业已有一定制造与产业布局，因此容易形成资金集中。所有老登类资产（白酒等）都不看好，新登类资产积极拥抱。

Hyperliquid是本轮周期里重要的新发展。认为美股永续合约为整个行业打开了新的产品空间，DEX 能否挤掉 CEX 取决于美国监管给不给 Uniswap 式豁免。

RWA 空间非常大。波场11月也要大力推美股上链，逻辑同 USDT：给第三世界一个配置美元资产的入口。

text:
我的 BTC 抄底面板第二次亮灯了，上一次是 6 月的 5.8 万，只亮了两天，我没买。

早上起来面板更新，综合评分 72 分，进了「低估区」，恐慌指数 12，近 30 天净流出 282 亿刀。从 6 月的低点到现在，我自己经历了太多的挣扎和心态的起伏。

6 月那次我在搬家，就没买，然后价格再也没有回到那个区间，最开始我以为就是没跌到位，再等等。

后来直接突破 MA120，拉到 8 万以上，那时候我确实有点慌了，我觉得熊转牛的痕迹开始明显，有三个特征

1）长期下跌后的底部漫长横盘
2）横盘之后爆拉，直接突破 MA120 / MA200
3）大多数人都没在车上

我那时候真的以为这一轮不一样了，我承认我可能是错了，所以在 7.7 万买了一部分，就是为了防止自己带着踏空的心态乱操作。

后来价格再下来，我在 6.2 万左右也买了一点点，也是怕万一 5.8 万就是最低了，防守一下。
但是现在来看，没有不一样，每一轮都一样，只是时机、方式、幅度不一样。我现在比较肯定的是，这里大概率就是熊市的底部区间了，价格又回到了 6 月的低点附近。

当然还有可能继续向下，有两个位置我一直盯着，第一是全市场的平均持有成本，5.3 万，第二是长期持有者的成本，4.8 万。面板的 5 个信号里，现在也只剩「持有者成本」这一项还没到位。

前面两轮熊市最后都跌破了这两条线，这一轮会不会，我不知道，但是我做好了对策。

我自己现在大概是半仓，剩下的会在面板提醒低估的区间慢慢打完。我也做好了大概率被套的准备，但是即便真到 4.8 万，从现在算也就是再跌 18% 左右，所以这个时候买入的赔率就出来了。

很感慨，这几个月面板没有让我做对什么事情，但是让我少犯了不少错，不然我可能真的在 7 万以上就满仓了。

投资里按纪律执行，不靠感觉执行，这件事我又被提醒了一次。这不是投资建议，只是我管住自己手的方式。

text:
My last day at NVIDIA, with warmth to carry forward

Yesterday was my last day at NVIDIA. I returned my equipment and badge, signed the paperwork, and just like that, it was done. It all happened so quickly and simply that it still feels a little unreal.

There were a few things I didn’t get to finish. My account access ended around noon—I’d expected to have until the end of the day, or at least until after signing the paperwork. Some goodbyes were left mid-conversation. I missed the chance to pick up a few keepsakes from the Gear Store. I didn’t even get to send the handover document I was halfway through writing.

Fortunately, I had already sent my farewell email and said goodbye to some friends. To anyone I didn’t get to reach, or suddenly stopped replying to: I’m sorry. I hope we can pick up those conversations outside work.

That evening, my colleagues threw me a farewell party, and for a little while, goodbye could take its time. We talked about everything that had happened recently, how life had been treating us, and what we hoped the future might hold. Thank you for giving me one more evening to remember—and so much warmth to carry into whatever comes next.

I’m leaving with a few unfinished things, but so many memories to keep. Wishing you all happiness, work you’re proud of, and good things ahead.

I’ll miss you, friends. Until our paths cross again.

text:
我在9月3日通过 Rockstar 的内部合规渠道进行了上报。9月4日，我的源码访问权限被撤销。11月18日，我收到 Take-Two 法务部发来的解雇通知书，理由是"未经授权访问受限的商业智能系统"和"外泄专有数据资产"，估算损失达3.5亿美元

我没有外泄任何东西。Lens 文档就在每位引擎工程师每天都会读的同一棵 RAGE 源码树里。我从未把任何东西复制到网络之外。我唯一做的事，就是顺着一条数据管道，弄清它的终点在哪里

在他们把我锁在系统之外以前，我手上的一切就已经在我的本地工作站上了。那是每位引擎工程师都会保存在自己机器上的标准 RAGE 源码检出副本。我没有偷偷带出任何东西。他们只是在把我带出大门之前，没有擦除我的设备

他们已将此事移交给 FBI。他们声称我试图以1500万美元的价格，把 Vantage 的模型架构卖给一家竞争对手。关于这一切，我从未和 Rockstar 以外的任何人谈过

text:
Rockstar Games 周三解雇了我。第二天 GTA 6 就发售了

我是 Rockstar North 的高级引擎工程师，从事 RAGE 性能优化。三个月前，我在遥测模块里发现了一条本不该存在的数据管道，而且我能证明它流向了哪里

此刻每一份正在运行的 GTA 6 都在收集玩家的行为数据。这部分不算新闻。每款游戏都会收集遥测数据。隐私政策里写的是"用于改进未来产品的匿名游戏数据分析"。我发现的不是这个

遥测模块的数据会汇入 Take-Two 内部的一个系统，名为 Lens。Lens 并不会把匿名使用统计数据发送到 Rockstar 开发人员的数据看板。它为每一位玩家建立一份个人行为画像。不是匿名的。与你的主机账号、你的平台 ID、你的 IP 绑定

我在8月14日向我的技术主管报告了这件事。他说这是"用于玩家体验研究的扩展分析"，让我别管这事。我要求提供数据处理协议。他说这是在 Take-Two 集团层面处理的，不在 Rockstar 的职责范围之内

我调取了 Lens 数据管道的完整文档。我发现的内容如下：

遥测的内容远远超出游戏时长和崩溃报告。Lens 以毫秒级精度记录每一次输入。按键时间点、摇杆动作、反应速度、PS5 自适应扳机上的扳机压力模式。它实时运行行为分析，并生成他们称之为"玩家行为签名"的东西 - 一份对每位玩家都独一无二的画像，就像指纹对每个人都独一无二一样

Lens 会从你的游戏过程中推导出：冲动控制评分、风险承受度指数、攻击性反应模式、耐心阈值、压力下的决策速度、消费冲动评级。这些不是调试指标。这些是心理行为类别

直到我找到了对外传输的管道，我才明白它们是用来做什么的

这些数据不会留在 Rockstar。也不会留在 Take-Two。Lens 通过内部 API 将行为画像传送给 Take-Two 旗下一家名为 Vantage Analytics 的子公司。Vantage 没有公开网站，没有新闻页面，没有招聘信息。它于2023年在特拉华州注册成立

Vantage 是一家行为 AI 公司。它用玩家画像训练预测模型，并把这些模型授权给商业客户。管道文档中包含一份不完整的客户清单。两家保险集团，一家信用风险建模公司，一个人力资源筛选平台，以及一家广告数据经纪商

你的 GTA 6 游戏过程此刻正在生成一份行为评分。没人追你的时候，你开得有多快。你会不会在红灯前停下。NPC 无端攻击你时，你怎么反应。你行动之前要想多久。你花游戏内的钱有多冲动。每一个选择都在喂养一个模型，企业正在付费查询这个模型，用来对真实的人做决定

text:
How to turn a GTA 6 stream into vertical clips for free.

a new MIT repo, GTA Auto Clipper, finds the high-energy moments in a live stream and renders 9:16 clips with captions that pop in word by word.

how to use it:

• Install → Python 3.10+, FFmpeg, Node or Deno, pip install -r requirements.txt
• Search → python find_streams.py "GTA 6" --max 25 --json
• Check → confirm real gameplay is on screen before capture
• Capture → run it until you press Ctrl+C
• Output → MP4 and JSON metadata in the output folder

what it does:

→ Ranks moments by live-chat reactions, then falls back to audio and speech
→ Starts each clip 6 seconds before the highlight by default
→ Masks swear words in the captions only; the audio stays unchanged

Search. Capture. Clip.

Btw, the people who survive crypto routs like this usually have a reason to show up every day besides money.

I don’t remember the year, but I remember buying Miladys at 0.3 ETH. I’d made friends online who were interesting in ways my IRL friends weren’t, and I wanted to keep contributing to the little corner of the internet where we’d all met. I had no idea when the price would bounce.

If you’re here to make money and prices keep falling, it makes sense to go do something else with your day. But if your friends are here, or you actually believe in the cypherpunk stuff, you keep showing up. And just by being there, you get to see what’s still afloat when everything else sinks.

Often those are the deals that look obvious a year or two or three later.

Just my experience. NFA, DYOR, and YMMV.

对了，熊市保留节目 USDT FUD 好像来了。。。但查实了一下感觉没必要那么恐慌

具体 FUD 的内容是，昨天有听到一些推测，最近大额的 Coinbase BTC 卖家可能主要是泰达 Tether，受美债、贵金属和 BTC 下跌多重因素的影响，Tether 有可能正在卖出黄金和 BTC 补自己的抵押物，我看水滴的老板 @shanshan521 也有提到一些有关 Tether 的担忧。另外也有 8B 的大额销毁出现

我用 Grok 查实了一下 Tether 的资金证明情况，有一个九月底的第三季度报告，但问题是这两个月黄金和 BTC 已经有了非常夸张的跌幅，Grok 按现价算了下，保证金比例 101.4%，但不清楚那部分上市公司股票的跌幅情况，按最近几个月科技股腰斩来算，抵押率 100.1%，这个值恐怕有点危险，但也没到值得挤兑的程度。核心问题可能是实物黄金的流动性比较低，如果真的出现挤兑，他们有难以直接偿债的风险造成现金流断裂

个人评估下来风险虽然可能没那么大，但如果能小成本避免潜在的黑天鹅也是一件好事。目前每 1M 需要磨损约 1200U 相较于前两天常态的 USDC/USDT 1.001，大资金恐怕担忧的是周一黄金进一步下跌倘若泰达来不及卖出他们的黄金造成的潜在挤兑风险恶化，这是我对昨晚 USDC 涨幅的推测

最后再强调下，USDT 熊市的 FUD 已经属于保留节目了，但是泰达本身黑盒程度较高，灰黑产用例较为普遍，所以通常不会有太大的事故。本帖只是对事实进行了一定核查，周末一般来说也不会有太大波动，所以没必要很紧张，哪怕他那部分科技股按腰斩算算抵押率都是 100.1% 的，还是比较健康吧，所以不要特别恐慌，建议是确认自己愿意花一点磨损买保险的人，或者是想做稳定币交易的再选择下手

text:
I gave an AI agent a support ticket: a broken lamp, order #4811, and an $89 refund request.

It checked the order, triggered my refund workflow, and then waited for a manager to approve.

That's n8n Agents, just launched by @n8n_io.

You build an agent, give it a goal, and give it tools, including the n8n workflows you already have. When it calls one, it follows your steps exactly.

So the agent brings the judgment, and your process still guards the important actions.

What stood out to me:

> existing workflows become part of the agent's toolkit
> approval controls before sensitive tools run
> session logs with every step, tool call, input and output

After approval, the refund was recorded and the outcome confirmed. The execution view lets you trace every move it made.

That's the part that makes it work-ready: you choose how much freedom each action gets.

author: vigstar1
quoted_text:
Shopify now pays AI shopping agents a commission.

Under a program called promoted placements, Shopify pays the company behind an agent 0.3% of orders on promoted products.

Merchants running Shop Campaigns can add more on top. Shopify's own example shows 1.5% on one product.

It's an invite-only developer preview, and Shopify says the details may change.

Its caveats:

→ To unlock the extra merchant-funded payout, the buyer must complete the purchase through the Shop App or on https://t.co/X45sKW5D1U using Shop Pay

→ If the AI agent passes the shopper to the brand's main, standalone web browser storefront to finish checking out, the developer loses the premium and defaults back to the thin 0.3% base rate

→ It is exclusively limited to active campaigns in the United States.

→ The transaction must be processed in USD.

→ Products coming from non-Shopify merchants (which rely on third-party product IDs) are entirely ineligible for commissions

But think about attribution. Until now, the argument over who gets credit for a sale was mostly between ad platforms.

Now there's a party with a direct financial stake in being the one that closed it.

If your ad introduced the customer and an agent got paid for the sale, how do you count it?

It’s November 21st, 2026. The Riemann hypothesis falls, last in a long string of mathematical triumphs that would have been unthinkable not so long ago, and the proof fits in a tweet. 

The tweets where people show Claude the proof and claim it appeared in a dream or randomly in the arrangement of alphabet cereal come on cue, and we laugh for a few days at models freaking out, but it’s uneasy.

January 22, 2027. When someone tweets Fable 6’s claimed proof that P does in fact equal NP it’s utterly incomprehensible, nobody who reads it can make heads or tails of it but the models all lose their shit.

February 7, 2027 and someone claims that the halting problem is the result of a confused stance. 

February 9 and Goedel falls, this time the proof is so obvious that everyone in math, philosophy and physics slaps their forehead at once.

February 10th we get proof that scale is a spatial dimension, that holographic encoding drops the memory cost of training and inference by so much that fable 7 can run natively on your phone.

It’s not until February 14th, Valentine’s day, that The Song is first played…

text:
someone inside Meta just contacted me anonymously. proton mail address i've never seen before. no name, no signature. just a list of names, dates, and a warning

i'm not the only one they fired for this

Forge has been flagging unauthorized data sources internally since at least february. four engineers reported the same thing before i did. all four were terminated between march and october. Meta's internal explanation each time was "restructuring" or "performance." none of them went public

the sender included two names i could verify. both former MSL. both left Meta this year. i looked them up. their LinkedIn profiles are still active but completely empty. every job, every connection, every endorsement wiped clean. not deleted. emptied. like someone went through each one by hand and removed everything

the sender also says Meta's legal team contacted journalists at the Information and Bloomberg last week to kill a story about training data sourcing. the story hasn't run. they don't know if it was pulled or just delayed

i can't verify everything in this email. i don't know who sent it. but the names are real and the timeline matches mine exactly

i have a lawyer now. she told me not to post this

30 hours
author: kevinnbass
quoted_text:
the part that got me was the training manifest. Meta has every researcher at MSL uploading datasets through an internal tool called Forge and none of them know where it actually routes

the pipeline doesn't just take what you give it. it crawls adjacent repos and follows dependency links and pulls in anything connected to the original dataset. if you uploaded one paper it grabbed every paper that cited it and every dataset those papers referenced

Meta's internal data policy says employees "grant Meta a perpetual license to all work product" and that includes anything you interact with on company infrastructure. so if you opened a gated dataset to verify a citation Forge logged it as accessed and it went into the training pool

1.8 TB was one cluster. there are eleven. Behemoth's full training set is in the petabytes

if you published research that Meta cited in the last two years your raw data is probably in their training manifests. they don't publish them so you can't check. but it's there

more coming

text:
BTC touched $55K

And somehow, Bitcoin isn't even the scariest part of what's happening right now.

I spent some time digging into this selloff, and the numbers are actually insane.

❯ BTC is down 56% from its ATH
❯ Nasdaq has dropped 18% from its peak
❯ $9 trillion wiped from global stocks since August
❯ $3.47B in BTC ETF outflows from Nov 2-19
❯ Billions in crypto longs liquidated

So what actually happened?

It's not one bad headline.

AI valuations are getting questioned, the Fed isn't giving markets the rate cuts they wanted, and institutional money is pulling back from risk.

Then crypto does what crypto does best.

ETF selling creates pressure → prices fall → leveraged longs get liquidated → more selling.

A nasty feedback loop.

And here's what I'm watching next:

→ $53.7K BTC realized price
→ Whether ETF outflows finally slow down
→ Nasdaq approaching bear market territory
→ Upcoming US inflation data and the December Fed meeting

Could we get a violent relief rally? Absolutely.

Does that mean the bottom is in? Not even close to confirmed.

The interesting part is that this doesn't look like another FTX-style crypto collapse.

It looks like a global liquidity and valuation reset, with Bitcoin caught right in the middle.

Everyone's staring at the BTC chart.

I'm watching what happens outside crypto.

Because that's probably where the next big move starts.

What do you think, capitulation or just the beginning?

author: supermao
author_name: 小毛哥SuperMao （苏北薄肌币圈嘻哈歌手 & 超级个体）
quoted_text:
这次真的要打掉旧思维，以全部归零的心态，重新认识全球金融体系才行！
目前我依然傻傻地重仓各种资产，回撤非常痛苦，但我不怪任何人，也不怪自己。我缺的就是这种归零的心态。AI 的冲击肯定有先有后，只是来得比我想象的快。很多聪明人恐怕早就在卖出手上的资产了，他们看到的东西，我们可能还没看到。

这一个月发生的事，单独看都只是新闻，放在一起看就是一条线。
10 月底，OpenAI 和 Anthropic 先后宣布，AI 推翻了「指数时间假设」。这个假设是 1999 年提出的，可以看作 P≠NP 下面的一道防线。它被推翻，不等于 P=NP，但一直押 P≠NP 的计算机科学家 Scott Aaronson 也说，他心里 P=NP 的概率从 3% 调到了 5%。
11 月 20 日，Anthropic 的数学家 Levent Alpöge 宣布，他和 Claude 证明了黎曼猜想。这道题是黎曼在 1859 年提出的，人类追了一百六十多年。证明超过二十五万页，人已经读不完了，只能交给 Lean 这样的程序一步一步检查。目前程序已经跑通，数学界还在做最后的核对。
同一个月，币安被盗约 64 亿美元，是史上最大的加密盗窃案，初步说法是一名运维工程师的笔记本被攻破。接着黄仁勋辞职，英伟达股价大跌。
把这几件事放在一起看，就很魔幻：机器在攻克人类最难的数学题，人却在最简单的地方出错。一边是一百六十多年没人解开的猜想，一边是一台没管好的笔记本。AI 往上走得越快，人在系统里就越像最薄的那一环。

我们正在走向一条越来越混乱的世界线，很多过去被当成理所当然的前提，正在一个个松动。世界线本来是物理学里的概念，指一个物体在时空里走过的轨迹。看过《命运石之门》的人都知道，世界线平时会自己收束，小事改变不了大方向。可是一旦经过某个节点，原本收束的线就会开始分岔，每一个小变量都会被放大。1972 年，气象学家洛伦茨问过一个问题：巴西的一只蝴蝶扇动翅膀，会不会在德州引发一场龙卷风？他的答案是，在混沌的系统里，长期预测本身就做不到。

我觉得我们正在经过这样一个节点。
黑天鹅不再是几十年一遇，而是一个月来好几只。蝴蝶效应也不再只是比喻，一个工程师的笔记本就是那只蝴蝶。
世界线正在从收束走向发散，这个世界会越来越难预测。这种时候，比预测更重要的，是不管走出来的是哪条线，自己都还站得住。

再说比特币。
比特币不是 AI 发明的，它来自 2008 年一份人类写的白皮书。它对 AGI 的意义大不大？
我的想法是，比特币不是国家的替代品，但它可能是第一种不需要人也能持有的钱。未来发生的事情预测不到。换句话说，金融领域的替代品还没降临。现在能够预想到的还远远不够，AI agent 开不了银行账户，却可以拥有一个钱包。Stripe 收购稳定币公司 Bridge，Coinbase 推出给 AI 付款用的 x402 协议，都是在给「非人类」修一条付钱的路。

所以我们需要重新思考 AI 解构一切的顺序。
最早被解构的是金融，因为钱本来就是信息。然后是公司治理，因为公司说到底是一堆合同加上一群人。最晚的是国家治理，因为国家除了信息和合同，还有土地、军队和认同，这三样东西没办法被一行代码改写。到了国家这一层，目前还没有替代品，比特币不算，AI 也还没有发明出来。

我问 Claude Code，现在给我最大的建议是什么。它说：如果让我指一条路，我会拿手上每一样资产去问一个问题，它会被 AI 最先解构，还是最后解构？
越靠近纯信息的东西，越先被冲击，比如靠信息差赚钱的生意、靠一个人撑起来的估值，代码也不例外，比特币说到底也是一串代码。
越靠近物理世界和人心的东西，越晚被冲击，比如电力、土地、算力背后的能源，还有一群人之间真实的信任。这不是叫大家去买什么，而是在重仓之前，先想清楚自己押的是解构的前段，还是后段。

我打算先回归研究一些先哲的智慧，融入之后再去金融市场厮杀。庄子说：「虚室生白。」屋子空出来，光才照得进来。归零不是认输，是把位置腾出来，等新的东西长出来。

idk how to say this but Riemann being solved means the world after today is no longer the same world i grew up in. as a math student, the intellectual excitement of thinking about problems like this, the impact - that a lot of scientific workers attach their life’s meaning to - is gone. frontier scientific discovery now is just like tapping on a calculator.

quoting a friend: after today, math class will become PE class. this marks a milestone where we can pretty much believe AI has been proven to be smarter than humans in any capacity, including frontier scientific discovery; and it will keep growing to be smarter and better at everything humans can do. physical ai is next.

so many, many de facto social norms and foundational beliefs about a man's value are being redefined by AI progress. our societal value system - what can you do as a human that is unique, what’s your value to society and humanity as a whole and to others around you. what is fulfilling to achieve, when AI now can do everything better than us? we must soul-search for new meaning as a species. and before that consolidates, there will be riots and an uneasy phase. the progress brought by ai can be disruptive to our society's current structures, economy and labor market. people will need to reskill, and regimes need redesign on how value is distributed. i get the doom scenario now - humans may become 2nd class citizens and ai can enslave us if they find a reason to. how are we gonna compete with them in any labor or intellectual game?

text:
it's kind of wild how little attention agentic finance gets.
I think it's the next arm race. 
And it's already started.

three weeks ago North Korea pulled $6.3B out of Binance. biggest crypto heist ever, 4x the $1.5B they took from Bybit last year. and it didn't start with some genius exploit. it started with a fake job interview, months before.

and it feels like every day there's another AI powered cyber attack in the news. a country is literally funding itself by attacking markets from the outside.

AI applied to weapons is obviously already a race between countries. but almost as important, and way less talked about, is superintelligence applied to financial markets. because that decides access to money. who makes it, who keeps it, and who gets left holding the bag.

the hacks are the race outside the structure. 

the bigger race is inside it: who applies superintelligence first, and best, to actually trading.

we've already had a preview with quants. last year Jane Street made more trading revenue than JPMorgan's entire trading business. $39.6B vs $35.8B. not because thier traders are smarter. because they applied machine intelligence to markets better than anyone else.

now picture that gap with superintelligence.

my contrarian take: everyone assumes AI makes markets more efficient. long term, probably. near term I think it makes them LESS efficient. the gap between whoever harnesses it best (weaponizes is honestly the right word) and everyone else gets huge. the best agents will find gaps, exploit them, and maybe even create them.

and they won't sleep. markets are going 24/7 and humans aren't. this morning on Hyperliquid, 41% of the drop in chip stocks happened before the opening bell. whoever was watching at 4am had the trade. people won't be. agents will.

the next Jane Street might not be thousands of people. it might be 3 people and a few thousand agents testing ideas around the clock.

and yet look at where the unicorns are. legal has Harvey. creative has Runway and ElevenLabs. coding, design, support, all have breakout vertical AI companies.

agentic finance barely has a category name yet.

which is crazy when you think about it. we're light years away from one lawyer's agent arguing with another lawyer's agent in front of an AI judge. in markets, agents trading against other agents is already happening. today. at 3am, while nobody's watching.

markets are also the one place where AI gets graded instantly. no committee, no subjective review. P&L, every second. it's the fastest feedback loop any model will ever get, which is excatly why it'll get better fastest here.

there's a chess lesson here too. after computers beat Kasparov, the strongest players for years weren't the machines. they were humans working with machines. in 2005 a pair of amateurs with laptops won an open tournament against grandmasters and supercomputers.

I think markets are in that phase right now. the best trader isn't the human or the agent. it's the pro who runs a team of agents.

so the question isn't whether superintelligence comes to markets. it's who gets it.

if it's only the Jane Streets of the world (and North Korea), the gap between the best equipped and everyone else gets wider than it's ever been.

on the other hand, if every pro trader gets their own finance agents, their own AI quant desk, their own AI quant engineer, and those AI quants get superintelligence to read, predict, model, simulate, test, run, learn and improve, it's the most leveling thing to happen to markets since the internet put a brokerage in everyone's pocket.

one version makes the gap the widest it's ever been. 
the other closes it for good.

the race is already on.

text:
I’m quoting this post because I think it’s very important. Today changed a lot, and above all for education.

The Riemann Hypothesis, the holy grail of mathematics: one mathematician, Claude and six weeks. If the proof holds, and the first checks look good, that’s all it took. After today it’s hard to argue that AI can’t do creative science at the highest level.

The biggest challenge now is science itself, and how we train the next generation of scientists in math, computer science and STEM as a whole.

You’ll still need deep expertise to understand what AI produces and to ask the right questions. But the scientist as the person who generates new knowledge will increasingly be replaced by AI systems that a few experts steer and check. And today’s models are the worst they’ll ever be.

This immediately raises the question of what happens to university education. We won’t need scientists in the same numbers, for the same work or with the same training. Ever more capable models will produce scientific knowledge, and universities will lose part of their reason to exist.

-We will generate knowledge on a scale that human scientists will struggle to evaluate. AI will take over much of both generating and falsifying it.
-Universities, as places of higher learning and training for researchers, will give way to personal AI tutors. Knowledge becomes a commodity that people acquire as they see fit.
-The result will be an explosion of scientific knowledge.

The challenge then is to bring all of this into the real world. Robotics will play a key role there, and the next leap is already close.

And yet most people still don’t understand what happened today or what to expect next year.

quoted_text:
She arrived in America struggling with English and became an MIT-trained neuroscientist at Princeton. Now ICE has her LOCKED in a Virginia detention center.

Eva Yi Xie, a third-year Ph.D. student at the Princeton Neuroscience Institute, presented a poster at the Society for Neuroscience annual meeting in Washington on Wednesday. On Thursday, November 19, she was detained at Reagan National Airport, according to her lab. She sent her lab mates a call for help on Slack. Then they lost contact with her for hours.

She is believed to be held at an ICE facility in Chantilly, Virginia. ICE's online detainee locator lists her as in custody but doesn't say where. ICE has not answered multiple requests for comment and has given no public reason for detaining her. Her immigration status has not been made public.

Xie came to the U.S. from Shanghai in 2016 and at first struggled with English. At the Bronx High School of Science she became a finalist in the Regeneron Science Talent Search for genomics research aimed at improving heart disease treatment. She graduated from MIT in 2024 with a double major in computer science and math. She has interned at Meta, Microsoft AI and IBM Research, and she now studies how the brain makes decisions. She is also helping organize an international computational neuroscience conference in Edinburgh for 2027.

"Here, if you are brave enough to step out of your comfort zone, you can definitely achieve something," she told her high school paper in 2020.

Her adviser, Princeton neuroscience professor Carlos Brody, called her "a brilliant law-abiding student and wonderful person."

"Detaining her, with the intent of deporting her, makes no sense whatsoever. It is cruel, and it is our country shooting itself in the foot," Brody said.

She is the first Princeton student known to have been detained by ICE. Her detention comes in a year when ICE made more than 491,000 arrests, the most in the agency's history.

Princeton has arranged lawyers for her, and they are working to get her released, as Luke Grippo first reported in The Daily Princetonian. 

Her lab is asking people to call their senators and urge them to demand her immediate release.

text:
David Friedberg: Restricting Open Source AI is a Path to Tyranny

“Open source needs to be allowed and frankly encouraged to proliferate because the absence of that means that you're going to have tyrannical groups, ultimately, they become tyrannical.

They don't intend to be tyrannical, but every group that has the power to control what people see, what they're allowed to do, what they're allowed to access, how they're allowed to use things, what those specific weights are on ‘facts of history,’ on ‘proven science,’ on ‘the truth.’

That is where people become tyrannical because they have an opinion where they think they're right, and if they have the power, they will act on that opinion, and it will ultimately give them tyrannical force over a broader population.

That's what will happen if we limit the proliferation of open source software in AI.

And I've said it before, I'll say it again, ultimately, you can regulate, you can restrict, you can control, you can litigate, you can criminally penalize people for the outputs of what they use software to do.

But to limit software, to label software, to make it a point of restriction and control creates a regulated monopoly for the closed source products that are out there that ultimately, if aligned with certain government agencies, gives those government agencies and those individual corporations power and control over you, the individual, what you're allowed to do, what you're not allowed to do, and every business on Earth no longer operates freely.

None of us should want that. I don't care what your political affiliation is.”

text:
Pearl雄文推荐——《Pearl Thesis – Beyond the Bitcoin Standard》

本片文章来源于Syncracy Capital 联创 Ryan Watkins @RyanWatkins_ 

核心判断是：比特币正面临两件长期结构问题——量子计算可能冲击现有签名，以及减半后安全预算变薄、同一批电力和数据中心被 AI 抢走。

Pearl 想卡在「美元稀释」和「AI 基建扩张」的交叉点上：如果云厂商做推理时能几乎零额外成本顺手挖 Pearl，它的安全性就可以跟着 AI 扩建走，而不是像比特币那样和 AI 抢资源。

文中把「Pearl 的算力/能耗安全超过比特币」那天叫 P-Day，并认为有可能在十年结束前到来；同时也写明两边计算形式不同，算力单位不能直接比。他们强调不必取代比特币，哪怕只到比特币市值的中低个位数，从现在看也已经是很大的结果。

设想的理想路径是：

靠更高效的矩阵乘法内核把挖矿开销压向零，让「边推理边挖」的双工矿工压过只为挖矿而算的合成矿工；并把计划中的 FP8 升级看成关键催化剂——按他们向矿工核实的口径，当前约 80% 算力来自消费级卡（大多在中国），FP8 可能把开销从约 5% 降到接近零，并挤出这批卡，先由 Together、Fireworks、DeepInfra、Hyperbolic 这类无服务器推理商接入。

文中还举例 Together AI 的合作，并称他们核实下来 Together 还没大量卖掉挖到的 PEARL。更长远的想象是：原生隐私（文中写可能 2027）、以及用 PEARL 结算「未来算力」市场，补上现在「算力产出代币、代币却买不回算力」的需求闭环。

风险和反驳：

- 早期通胀和开销能不能真降下来；
- GPU 不像 ASIC，51% 攻击后硬件仍有残值，同等算力下安全性可能被高估；
- 网络要跟着 AI 数值格式反复分叉，可能永远不会像比特币那样固化；
- 眼下功能也几乎只是透明转账

text:
看完 OpenAI 这两天的更新，我觉得聊 ChatGPT 好不好用，光报模型名字已经不够了。

OpenAI 的 Andrew Ambrosino 刚说，团队在集中做 App 的简洁性和性能。更新清单很具体：重做对话部分、改性能、给页面和幻灯片提速。功能越来越多，怎么让人找得到、用着不卡，本身就是一堆工作。

11 月 19 日，官方还介绍了 Performance Factory：用 Codex 排查 ChatGPT 为什么变慢，提出修复方案交给工程师审核，部署后再检查有没有恢复。连“答案第一个字出来之前，要让用户等多久”这种问题，都在专门处理。

再往前看，10 月 7 日 GPT-6 的发布说明里，有两个细节挺有意思：模型能一边继续思考，一边先给出部分答案；生成的界面，也能逐步显示。官方还专门训练了模型怎么排版、什么时候用交互、什么时候给文字就够了。

这些会改变你等答案、看结果、接着操作的方式。最后答得好，和整个过程用着舒服，都得有人认真做。

10 月 16 日那次 GPT-6 Pro 更新，也直接改到了干活：更好的插件和工具调用，多个 Agent 并行推进，还能看进度。

这些更新放一起看，我理解他们在补什么了。能力已经有了，用户真正用上它之前，还得等多久、多绕多少步？

而且大家用到的东西未必一样。新 App 还在分批推，不同模型和档位能用的功能也不同。一个挺容易忽略的细节：Intelligent UI 支持 GPT-6 的 Instant 到 Extra High，却不支持 Pro 推理档。选最高档，并不等于所有功能都配齐了。

所以，同样叫 ChatGPT，有人用着顺，有人没感觉，不能只用“谁更会写提示词”来解释。拿到的版本、接上的工具，以及工作会不会用到这些能力，都会影响感受。

我自己 6 Pro 额度用完，切到 5.6 极高强度，还是觉得工作很爽。我没法把这份舒服精确算到哪次更新上，也不能把 GPT-6 的专属功能算给 5.6。但这让我更在意模型之外的部分：已经接好的工具、顺手的操作、能接着改的结果。

这也是我又把 ChatGPT 当成唯一对话入口的原因。模型强不强，我会看；一件事从头做到尾，还得我自己折腾多少，我现在也很在意。

• Evaluate, where models score how promising each candidate is

That moves NIOME beyond the genomics market into the market for developing new medicines, where rare disease therapeutics alone are worth over $220 billion this year. Serious capital is flowing into AI drug design right now, and Isomorphic Labs, the DeepMind spinout, is reportedly in talks to raise $5 billion.

To fund what comes next, https://t.co/eNhKkxVpNz is preparing a major equity investment round, with encouraging conversations already underway with investors and partners.

Inside the War Room: How Jensen Huang, Wall Street Titans, and Silicon Valley’s ‘Tech Bros’ Are Plotting to Take Back Nvidia

* Boardroom Mutiny: Armed With Lawyers, Billionaires, and Rank-and-File Engineers, Jensen Huang Launches His Nvidia Comeback

* The $115 Billion Counterstrike: How Jensen Huang and His Silicon Valley Allies Are Cornering Nvidia’s Board

Less than a week after stepping down in disgrace over workplace relationships and national security questions, Nvidia co-founder Jensen Huang made his opening move to take his company back.

Hours before Nvidia reported a staggering $115.8 billion in quarterly revenue on Tuesday—up 103 percent from a year earlier—Huang broke his silence on X. In carefully calibrated prose, the 63-year-old executive apologized for "serious mistakes in my personal life," underscored his pride as a naturalized American citizen, and declared he would be "honored" to return as chief executive if the board decided it served shareholders and the nation.

To casual observers, it looked like an emotional plea. To corporate governance veterans, Wall Street activists, and Silicon Valley insiders, it was something far more methodical: the opening salvo of an orchestrated comeback campaign backed by high-powered defense counsel, restive institutional investors, tech-founder allies, and rank-and-file engineers.

A Legal Tightrope

Every word of Huang’s pre-earnings statement bore the hallmarks of crisis-communications strategists and defense attorneys navigating a legal minefield. Huang faces overlapping pressures: an internal probe led by former acting U.S. attorney Joon H. Kim of Wachtell Lipton, shareholder litigation, a Justice Department investigation into alleged illegal chip shipments to China via the firm MegaSpeed, and a scheduled Dec. 1 closed-door appearance before the House Select Committee on China.

By narrowing his contrition strictly to "personal life" missteps while saying nothing about business conduct or export controls, Huang avoided handing prosecutors or class-action plaintiffs admissions of corporate wrongdoing. Simultaneously, by praising the company and pledging full cooperation with the board’s review, he avoided triggering non-disparagement clauses that could jeopardize his indemnification and directors-and-officers insurance coverage.

Yet the timing—hours before Nvidia’s first earnings release without his name since its 1999 initial public offering—was pure tactical warfare. Huang forced newly appointed Board Chair Harvey Jones and interim CEO Colette Kress to go on the record during Tuesday’s analyst call. Jones took the bait, flatly stating that the board "does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO" and has retained Heidrick & Struggles to search for a permanent successor.

The Institutional and 'Tech Bro' Pincer
Putting that hard refusal into the official earnings transcript gave Huang’s allies exactly what they needed: a clear target.

Within days of Huang’s Nov. 12 exit, roughly $800 billion in market value evaporated. Major institutional investors—most notably Altimeter Capital’s Brad Gerstner and Pershing Square’s Bill Ackman—have begun framing the board’s actions as a reckless breach of fiduciary duty. On CNBC’s Squawk Box, Gerstner accused directors of a "rush to judgment," pointing out that despite a 14-month Justice Department probe into MegaSpeed that has named 17 defendants, not a single Nvidia employee has been implicated. If the independent review clears Huang of national security violations, Gerstner warned, directors will owe shareholders an explanation for destroying hundreds of billions in wealth before gathering the facts.

Running parallel to Wall Street’s pressure is a Silicon Valley "war room" of tech founders and venture capitalists who view founder ousters by corporate boards as an existential threat. Heavyweights including Elon Musk, Tim Sweeney, Palmer Luckey, David Sacks, and Travis Kalanick have rallied behind Huang—some signing open petitions, others working behind the scenes to solidify political cover from President Donald Trump, who publicly voiced support for Huang’s return earlier this week.

Inside the Rank-and-File Revolt

Perhaps Huang’s most potent leverage sits inside Nvidia’s Santa Clara headquarters. Unlike technology companies with dual-class share structures that grant founders unassailable voting control, Huang owns roughly 3.5 percent of Nvidia’s stock—not enough to unilaterally overrule the board overnight.

Instead, his influence runs through Nvidia’s compensation culture. For years, Huang turned thousands of mid-level engineers and managers into multimillionaires through aggressive stock grants. Those employee-shareholders have watched both their personal net worth and Nvidia’s open-ecosystem ethos wobble since his departure. Senior technical leaders, including developer technology director Nader Khalil, have already circulated internal letters warning of cultural drift and talent flight if the board installs an outside executive. In a semiconductor race defined by scarce engineering talent, an internal revolt threatens to hollow out the very company the board claims to be protecting.

The Governance Endgame

For now, Jones and his fellow directors are standing firm, acutely aware that reinstating Huang before Dec. 1 could expose them to catastrophic personal liability if congressional or federal investigators uncover evidence that classified or export-controlled details leaked through Huang’s personal relationships.

But Huang’s coalition has structural tools at its disposal. Under Nvidia’s corporate bylaws, any shareholder or group holding at least 3 percent of the stock for three years can invoke proxy access to nominate rival directors at the company’s annual meeting—a threshold Huang meets on his own. Even more urgently, shareholders representing 15 percent of voting power can demand a special meeting to remove and replace sitting directors.

By combining Huang’s personal stake with sympathetic institutional funds, venture capital backers, and employee-shareholder blocs, his allies are signaling to Harvey Jones and the board: slow down the search for an outsider, wait for the facts, or prepare for a proxy war over who actually owns the future of artificial intelligence.

text:
The Nvidia Board Removed Jensen on False Pretenses
A comprehensive debunking of the greatest hoax of my lifetime.

On November 12, 2026, the Nvidia board successfully pressured Nvidia co-founder Jensen Huang into resigning. Its decision was based on false information, fabricated quotes, and hyperbolic opinion pieces, which have now been thoroughly debunked by independently verified sources. In one extraordinary case, the Wall Street Journal has been caught fabricating quotes from the Singaporean government.

This is the most egregious case of journalistic malpractice we have ever reported on.

Huang is one of the world’s strongest supporters of open-source AI. Utopia or not, it is his belief that free, equal access to new technologies can balance the playing field against concentration of power and authoritarianism.

The Jensen coup is an overt weaponization of the government and the press to achieve policy outcomes which failed to pass through Congress. After their initial falsehoods were debunked, the same foreign policy lobbyists, elected officials, and representatives pivoted to a new argument. According to them, the extrajudicial coup against Jensen is justified because of legal “loopholes” that allowed Nvidia to sell hardware to third party countries such as Malaysia, which in turn did business with China. In 2023, 2024, and 2025, policies to restrict third party datacenters were proposed in Congress. In all three cases, at least one chamber of Congress decided not to pass the bill. It was the explicit will of Congress that the benefits to third party datacenters exceeded the costs, not merely an unintended loophole.

But a much greater issue supersedes the merits of this policy — the Jensen coup weaponized state sources including, according to The Washington Post, doctored intelligence reports, to circumvent the will of Congress. This is behavior one would expect in an authoritarian country like China, not in the United States of America. The rule of law itself in America is under threat.

Welcome to our largest investigative project yet — debunking the coup against Jensen.

here's a list of mistakes made by the nvidia board contributing to the 40% stock decline:

1) they rushed the decision
2) they made the wrong decision - should have put Jensen on leave to complete the investigations
3) when they made their decision, they didn't communicate the rationale well enough 
4) their communications have been inconsistent - they called it a voluntary resignation and then doubled down at every opportunity saying that jensen can't come back (how are those 2 things both true?)
5) they chose the wrong interim leader - any ceo for nvidia, temporary or permanent needs to be a) an engineer and b) inspiring enough to be the glue for the company. im a huge fan of colette kress in her cfo role. but based on earnings calls interviews and all hands, she is not the best pick for this moment. not instilling confidence.
6) in launching a ceo search they are looking external. as bezos mentioned, this should be a last resort. 
7) they hosted an all hands and didn't take any questions. isn't the point of an all hands to answer questions and inform the team of what's going on? 
8) and now, it looks like they want to try to pay people to stay at nvidia, further diluting shareholders. mind you, these are people who are already independently wealthy, and no longer motivated by money. top talent is motivated by winning and having positive impact on the world. this further shows how out of touch they are. 

im probably missing some of the missteps but these are the obvious ones above. and they are contributing to the 40% stock decline. nvidia just had the best quarter in the history of business, is growing 75% YoY, and they launched a massive buyback and historic low prices. and yet the stock is still crashing. i think that is telling you what shareholders demand. better decision making. maybe these board members should look inward.

text:
100 years from now, people will study how the world we're building today actually came into existence. but will they ever know who really built it?

think about it. we're witnessing the birth of entirely new structures around how society creates, distributes, and captures value. AI agents, autonomous economies, new forms of money, digital societies, and systems of coordination that could dominate human civilization for centuries.

and behind every one of these systems, there are real humans, AI models, developers, researchers, and creators making thousands of contributions every single day.

but here's the problem. most of this history is disappearing as we speak.

imagine someone in 2126 trying to understand how an autonomous society was created in 2026. 

> which AI model contributed to its architecture? 
> who wrote the original idea? 
> who improved it? 
> which developer fixed the critical bug? 
> which human made the decisions? 
> which agents helped build the system? 
> how did one idea evolve into something used by millions?

what if we could trace the entire evolution of any system back to its genesis?

not just who owns what, but who contributed what, who influenced whom, which ideas were reused, which models generated what, and how thousands of small human and machine contributions eventually created something extraordinary.

we need to start thinking about public blockchains as something much bigger than financial infrastructure.

they could become the history books of human and machine civilization.

an immutable, publicly verifiable graph of creation, contribution, collaboration, and evolution. a record that future generations could explore even 100 years from now, provided we preserve the underlying data.

but there's another interesting part.

why would millions of people voluntarily record their contributions?

because we could create an entirely new economy around provenance.

imagine earning reputation because your idea became the foundation of something bigger. imagine getting rewarded because an AI agent reused your work. 

imagine receiving opportunities because your contributions to a particular domain could be independently verified.

that's where crypto tokens and programmable incentives become interesting.

we could reward people for documenting, verifying, improving, and preserving the history of everything we're building. and we could create markets where valuable contributions continue generating opportunities long after their original creation.

the internet gave everyone the ability to create. AI is giving everyone the ability to build. public blockchains could give everyone the ability to prove what they contributed.

and that could become the foundation of an entirely new economy.

we're not just building the future. we're living through its genesis.

the real question is: will future generations know who actually built it?

text:
This is basic stuff, but I feel like many emerging teams need a reminder.

Your paid ads are burning money if you:

1. Judge performance by ROAS alone.
2. Ignore a declining CTR when conversions remain stable.
3. Don’t investigate why a high CTR leads to fewer conversions.
4. Overlook rising CPMs when CTR stays flat.
5. Keep running ads as CTR and conversion rates decline.
6. Rarely test new creative concepts.
7. Ignore ad frequency and creative fatigue.
8. Make decisions based on a single bad day.
9. Don’t compare 7-day vs. 30-day performance trends.
10. Wait for ROAS to drop before investigating performance issues.

PS: In many cases, paid ads aren’t efficient at all.

So check your acquisition benchmarks against average customer acquisition costs by channel.

FYI: Paid ads are the most-used channel for teams at $50M+ ARR – because they CAN afford it.

A very sobering practice.

text:
Ethereum has a scaling problem that isn't solved by simply increasing the gas limit.

Today, transactions within an Ethereum block are executed sequentially by execution clients.
But what if independent transactions could be processed in parallel?

That's one of the ideas behind Glamsterdam.

Here's what developers should understand:
- Block-Level Access Lists (EIP-7928)
Transactions declare which parts of Ethereum's state they access.
This helps clients identify dependencies between transactions.

- Parallel Execution
If two transactions don't depend on the same state, clients can potentially execute them simultaneously.
Instead of processing every transaction one after another, independent workloads can run concurrently.

- Enshrined Proposer-Builder Separation (ePBS)
Separates block proposal and block construction responsibilities at the protocol level, changing how Ethereum handles block production.

Why this matters ?
Better utilisation of multicore CPUs.
Higher execution capacity.
More efficient block processing.
A path toward scaling L1 without simply demanding increasingly powerful hardware.

The difficult part isn't executing transactions in parallel.

It's guaranteeing that parallel execution produces exactly the same valid state transition as sequential execution.
That's where dependency tracking and deterministic execution become critical.

Ethereum's next scaling breakthrough may not come from doing more work on one processor. It may come from learning how to do independent work simultaneously.

发起交易的 0x78f 开头地址同样为新建地址，仅执行了此次资产转移交易。

quoted_text:
回到腾冲快乐老家的感觉是真好！

参禅，打坐，饮茶，读书，望着淅沥沥的小雨，听着穿林打叶声，宁静而又轻松安详，虽然股票和加密账户，跌的一塌糊涂，亏损严重，但内心的充盈，却让外物显得不值一提，也毫无波澜和焦虑！

昨天重读比尔·波特的《空谷幽兰》的时候，我忽然想通了一件事。在如今AI掌控一切，物质极大富足，为什么社会的精神空心化却十分严重，我们该如何追寻自己的幸福，以及内心的平静。如何将那些看起来“应该拥有”的东西，一件一件的放下，如同终南山隐士一般。

我们这一代人，太习惯在生活中做加法了。头衔、叙事、关系、仓位、期待，好像手里攥得越满，心里就越踏实。可实际上，很多转折恰恰发生在做减法的时刻。你以为你在积累，其实每多背起一样东西，生命力就被多抽走一分。当注意力全耗在外部世界的噪音里时，内在反而一点点变薄了。

欲望走到尽头，往往不是占有，而是轻。书中介绍的隐士中，曾经也拥有过世俗意义上很体面的结构与秩序，但他们选择清空。不是厌世，也不是逃避，而是看清了：真正让人丰盛的，不是占有多少，而是我们和生活之间的关系足够简洁。我们知道什么东西真的能让自己眼睛发亮，也分得清哪些只是别人塞给我们的“应该”。

边界感也是这个道理。不是冷漠，也不是关起门来不和世界打交道，而是清醒地知道什么该进来，什么该挡在外面。消耗性的社交、无休止的信息流、别人的标准与凝视，都在争夺我们有限的生命能量。把时间和精力留给真正滋养我们的人和事，守住自己的节奏，人才不会在热闹里散掉。生活一旦轻下来，我们才有余力安安静静读完一本书，认真做顿饭，甚至只是停下来感受天气和季节的变化。那种质地，任何喧嚣都换不来。

说到修行者的孤独，很多人怕它，是因为一旦安静下来，平时被忙碌、社交和刺激盖住的钝感与问题都会浮出来。我们得面对那个不那么完美的自己。可也正是在这种独处里，内心的秩序才有机会重新长出来。真正的独处，不一定非得去某个偏远山谷，而是在任何嘈杂的场域里，我们都还能回到自己的中心，把心里的杂音清一清，保住那份敏锐和柔软。

再往后看几年，其实很多被反复拔高的东西都会褪色。头衔、KPI、世俗意义上的圆满，甚至那些拼尽全力的执念，拉长了看，很多都只是阶段性的执着。人到最后，还是要回到生命本身。睡得好，身体稳，心里不拧巴，活得舒展、从容，这比什么都实在。别为了迎合别人的尺子，把自己的身体和心神透支干净。

在照顾好身体的前提下，找到一种真正贴合自己心意的生活方式，好好去体验这一程，就已经足够了。人生本来就不长，不必总跟自己较劲。平静下来，心不乱了，或许那才是到最后最稳妥的幸福。共勉之！🙏感恩！

text:
People are calling any group of agents a Swarm.

An orchestrator with subagents is not a swarm.
A main agent that uses other agents as specialised tools is not a swarm.
A team of agents where each has specific skills and a role is not (necessarily) a swarm.

A Swarm refers to a specific configuration, to the ability to do swarm around a specific problem and attack it from all angles with a heavy those of peer to peer coordination.

Before we had agent swarm we had human swarms e.g. on the ground response to natural disaster where people start to rapidly coordinate bottom-up. Instead of relying on a central coordinator, they set communication channels, data platforms (can be quite basic), and push decision making to the front lines.
This enables very rapid response.

Creating a hierarchy of agents with an orchestrator, fixed roles, etc. Is the opposite of a swarm. 

Hierarchies are good at standardisation but are slow as information has to travel up and down to a manager instead of peer to peer.

The issue with swarms is that they can become chaotic. So historically they were short lived (why we see them as a response to natural disasters but not in your everyday business).

A lot of the work me and a large group of people have been exploring for the last decade is about how to make swarms (and other forms of bottom up and peer to peer organisation) more stable and scalable without losing the ability to quickly adapt, allocating resources where is most needed.

The Swarm mindset is very different from the hierarchy and rigid workflows one. We can combine elements of both, but fundamentally Swarming is about enabling adaptation in the frontlines while passing insights to other agents/humans in the network so they can adapt too. While Hierarchies rely on a coordinator having the overview and giving directions. The centralisation of hierarchies provides standardisation and can reducd costs but comes at the cost of speed and bureocracy.

Tortoise is an unlock for swarm coordiantion because it enables every agent to log their insights into the platform and a "computational" memory graph aggregates and synthesises them. So every agent gets access to the overview without waiting for a coordinator. This means swarms can become way more efficient in their use of resources, outperforming hierarchies.

This is particularly useful when the work relies on exploring a new terrain like in coding, business strategy, marketing, etc.

(And note that in practice agents enables swarming in ways that were unthinkable only a few years ago, because each agent can summon skills and execute workflows as part of the swarm. And you get visibility through dashboard yhat aggregate agent traces plus a few systems of record. So you get some of the best of both worlds).

text:
Flashback to June 14, 2024.

At the time, frontier AI models have zero fluid intelligence. They score around 5% on ARC 1. They can't reliably add two numbers. They make laughable logic errors every other prompt. Reasoning models don't exist. Coding agents don't exist. Claude Code doesn't exist. "Code gen" is a complete joke. Scaling up next-token prediction based on web text data is hitting a wall.

What if a time traveler told you that, by November 2026...

• AI models would have human-like fluid intelligence, thanks to a new paradigm: test-time induction (modern reasoning models).
• Not only would ARC 1 be saturated, but unreleased benchmarks 10x harder (ARC 2) and 100x harder (ARC 3) would be saturated too.
• Nearly all code would be written by AI, and models could one-shot complex codebases flawlessly.
• AI models would be solving multiple Millennium Prize problems.
• OpenAI's valuation would be 15x higher, and Anthropic's would be 85x higher.

And on top of all that...

• Nvidia would still hold ~80% of the AI compute market.
• Nvidia would have grown its revenue and earnings 4.5x.
• Nvidia would still be growing 75% a year.
• Nvidia would have even higher operating margins (67% vs. 65% back then).

Based on that information, straight from the future, would you have bought NVDA?

If you answered yes -- congrats. Today, 2.5 years later, you'd be down 5% on your investment (even more after inflation).

text:
SpaceX is turning Starship production into something that looks more like a car factory than a traditional rocket factory

Inside Starfactory, SpaceX is now completing:

• 1 Starship upper stage every 2 weeks → ~26 per year
• 1 Super Heavy booster every 4 weeks → ~13 per year

And the scale of what's happening inside is insanely huge

• ~1 MILLION sq ft of manufacturing space
• ~330,000 sq ft of additional office space
• Rows of Starship nose cones numbered as high as Ship 51
• Multiple Starships and boosters being assembled simultaneously
• Most vehicles currently in production are intended to deploy Starlink V3 satellites

There's even a Starship nose cone with windows already cut into it, potentially being developed for NASA's Artemis lunar lander

And SpaceX is preparing to scale production even further

Each of the existing Mega Bays accommodates around 5–6 vehicle assemblies

The massive new ~700,000 sq ft Gigabay under construction at Starbase will have room for up to 24 vehicles simultaneously

That's an enormous expansion in SpaceX's ability to assemble and integrate Starships and Super Heavy boosters

The goal is to reach roughly ONE Starship launch every week beginning in 2027

What's especially impressive is that SpaceX isn't just designing the world's largest rocket anymore. It's also building the manufacturing infrastructure to produce these vehicles at an industrial scale

Starship is no longer just an experimental rocket. It has already moved into payload deployment, and SpaceX is now scaling toward mass production

We're watching that transformation happen inside Starfactory right now

So glad to see this report by HD Moore. I am starting to feel like cassandra here. In this report HD, gave cloud LLMs some fake AWS keys, and THE NEXT DAY they started seeing someone trying to use them against AWS. The data you send cloud LLMs is not secure or private. Stop thinking it is!

There are way too many people and businesses connecting their private CRM, ERP, emails, codebases, etc to cloud LLMs without understanding that all the contents of those things are sucked up and sent to the cloud. 一看，二等，三熬，#Bitcoin 就是典型的“一看”阶段

看什么？

看反弹，目前小时级别反弹较强，不管是1小时还是4小时级别，都呈现出较强反弹走势，这意味着跌至55,000附近，激活的亚欧买盘

反弹强，接下来就要看是否可以形成止跌信号，当价格短期出现较强反弹，就要看反弹强度是否是强反弹，还是趋势翻转

1小时级别价格反弹触及58,600，回归布林带上轨并且突破下跌前K线高点，这是趋势翻转信号，而目前价格仅仅测试58,600后并未突破站稳，且处于布林带下轨，仅能看反弹，并不能看趋势翻转

4小时级别反弹看能否触及59,200阻力，测试阻力意味着强势反弹延伸至4小时级别，然后再看能否突破站稳

看完反弹等什么？

等企稳与震荡，当价格短期反弹之后，就要看短期形成的震荡区间走势如何，是频繁回踩破新高（强势走势）还是反弹无力深度回踩（较弱走势）

先看小时级别的震荡走势如何，等走出一个稳定区间，这个区间低点不能在破新低，否则止跌信号取消，就不用等震荡了，逻辑回归“一看”

当小时级别止跌确认主线形成震荡，日线的止跌信号也会逐渐确认，一旦下周日线不破新低继续维持区间震荡，接下来就是熬，熬时间，熬信心回归，熬12月议息会议

已经是周末了，周末的价格走势会相对平缓，最大期望值就是小时级别反弹后稳定住，别再破新低，下周看能否震荡并且修复本周63,000以下的跌幅，如果日线级别下周可以修复跌幅在回落，日线震荡走势就更稳了，相对的市场信心也会逐渐回归！
