Jeveration overturns the rules of image generation: a single forward pass, no slow diffusion, no autoregressive steps. Just a frozen 4B Qwen3.5 VLM, lightweight adapters, and 128 parallel decision tokens—each one responsible for a piece of the image, all coordinated by a shared random state for global coherence.

The result: 512×512 images in 78 ms on an H200—122× faster than Janus-Pro-7B, and 5–8× quicker than the best diffusion accelerators. Quality? 0.74 GenEval, 78.2 DPG, 28.1 HPSv2.1—competitive with much slower models.

And it’s not just text-to-image. The same checkpoint handles edge/depth/style guided image-to-image and dense prediction (67.7 mIoU on NYUv2) in one pass, with no trade-off.

Jeveration shows that “System One” parallel decision models can generate and perceive images instantly, opening the door to real-time, on-device multimodal agents and ultra-fast creative tools.

text:
➥ Project Spotlight - Week 47/2026

Here are 9 projects worth a closer look.

➢ @tokastra
➢ @laserbeamxyz
➢ @supermassivedex
➢ @credditxyz
➢ @leaps_finance
➢ @Street__app
➢ @derpetual
➢ @SmartXTerminal
➢ @crshmarket

Here's what they do, and what could set them apart.

…

— | Tokastra

Tokastra makes it easier to compare the same stock across Ondo, xStocks, Robinhood, Coinbase, and other platforms. Its screener brings prices, issuers, and onchain volume into one place, saving you from jumping between sites.

…

— | Laserbeam

Laserbeam lets you describe a strategy in plain English, then have an AI agent backtest it and trade around the clock. Guardrails built into the protocol limit what it can do with your funds. It's planned as a launch app on @LayerZero_Core ATLAS and isn't live yet.
…

— | Supermassive

Supermassive is a planned @Solana derivatives venue from @temporal_xyz. Apps and market makers compete for orders, while one shared onchain clearinghouse holds collateral, letting you open a position through one venue and close it through another. Perps and spot come first, with options, dated futures, and prediction markets planned after.

…

— | Creddit

Creddit is a credit analytics, it helps you look beyond headline APYs. Its onchain fixed-income terminal covers repo lending, carry and looping strategies, and money-market-style funds, showing actual yield against SOFR, a US dollar benchmark rate, alongside utilization and collateral risk.

…

— | Leaps Finance

Leaps is a Solana options protocol where you earn upfront premiums by selling (not buying) options. Deposit SOL/cbBTC to sell covered calls, or USDC to sell cash-secured puts. Market makers bid via an onchain auction and the premium hits your wallet immediately; at expiry you either sell/buy at the strike or get your collateral back. Positions can’t be closed early.

…

— | Street

Street is building a market for private-company shares with sales approved by the companies themselves. You get direct ownership without SPV fund layers or carry fees. Access is opening to selected accredited investors and funds.

…

— | Derpetual

Derpetual offers "abstract futures": leveraged bets on almost any number, with longs and shorts settling directly against each other without an order book or market maker. Its partner app Derp is live on memecoins and reports over $4M in volume, and one founder is a @thielfellowship.

…

— | SmartX

SmartX brings social posts and onchain trading into one app. Trader profiles show real positions and profit and loss, and you can trade straight from a post in one tap, with fiat funding available too. It's in closed beta with zero trading fees during the beta, and says it's backed by @yzilabs.
…

— | CRSHMARKET

CRSHMARKET turns livestream moments into quick yes/no prediction markets on @monad, from esports to IRL streams. It announced a $3.5M seed round that included Reciprocal Ventures and reports 80K users and $20M in volume, both team-reported figures.

text:
比特币的 “ 四年周期” 一直被人讨论不休。

先说观点：比特币是一种大宗商品，但叠加了科技股属性。

2025 年，不少聪明的分析师都说比特币不会跌破 8 万、不会跌破 7 万，四年周期已经失效。

但从现在的走势看，四年周期依然有效，价格正在朝着周期对应的位置修正。

甚至正在向 @wolfyxbt 狼总2025年时算的狼波周期靠拢。

我基本同意 @uxuykevin 提到的“比特币是一个类似大宗商品”的说法，想在这个基础上补充一点：比特币在大宗商品之上，还叠加了科技股属性。

一个资产是什么属性，取决于谁在持有它。

过去，持有比特币最多的是币圈自己的人。就像原油主要握在产业链上的人手里，行业内的人持有行业内的资产，这是典型的大宗商品特征。

这两年，持有美股的人和持有比特币的人，越来越是同一批人。他们通过 ETF 买比特币，既看 AI，又看加密——这一类人是“科技新贵”。比特币也就带上了科技股的属性。

这就是为什么最近比特币和美股同涨同跌。比特币 7×24 小时交易，遇到极端下跌时，这批投资者往往先卖比特币，拿钱去给美股补仓。

类似的剧本，甚至也发生在黄金身上。

黄金本来是公认的避险资产，现在却越来越多地和美股同涨同跌，反而有了风险资产的味道。

原因也一样：越来越多人买黄金，图的是收益，避险反倒成了次要的。

顺着「谁在持有」这个思路，可以推出三个有意思的结论。

一、比特币和黄金是美股的先行指标。

它们会比美股更早做出反应。当比特币和黄金同步跳水时，往往说明背后还藏着更大的流动性危机。

二、比特币抛售的终点，就是比特币回归大宗商品属性的起点

大规模抛售之后，同时重仓美股的那批投资者会逐渐离场，留下来的又是币圈原本的人，比特币重新回到大宗商品属性。

三、比特币下跌的终点，就是美股危机的起点。

当比特币和黄金的抛售达到顶点，也意味着这批投资者的流动性接近枯竭，美股真正的危机才刚开始。

一言以蔽之：
1. 这一轮，比特币可能正在经历由美股资金主导的最后一次抛售。
2. 比特币的低点，很可能对应着美股危机的起点。
3. 等到美股哀鸿遍野的时候，就是比特币走出独立复苏的时候。

牢记一句话：持有者的属性决定了资产的属性，持有者的心理决定了资产的价格。

—— 救赎之道，就在其中。

@uxuycom 是第四年。

老朋友、新朋友都欢迎，只要你还在这个行业里。

text:
🚨 A domain controller can stay online while its database is stolen. A wallet’s private key can stay on the device while the money moves out.

In the November 21 edition of GCSA Insights, we break down five incidents that show how much damage follows when trusted systems are turned against their users.

1. VMware vCenter — Domain controller database stolen
ARMORY CASTLE exploited a vCenter zero-day to gain administrative access, reached an ESXi host, and extracted the Active Directory database from a virtual disk.

2. Wagyu XMR1 — 13.51 million USDC cashed out
The attacker moved 5.2 million XMR1 and sold 369,623 tokens on Hyperliquid. XMR1 fell from roughly $500 to $1.

3. Fluidkey — At least $1.58 million traced across six chains
Fluidkey says a third-party logging tool exposed session data. Unauthorized transactions were signed when users opened the app, then broadcast through Fluidkey’s own relayer. The private keys stayed on users’ devices.

4. Cisco Expressway — Four cluster nodes compromised
An intrusion at a Russian company spread from two internet-facing appliances to two internal nodes in the same cluster.

5. Apache Roller — The off switch came too late
Affected versions processed XML-RPC requests before checking whether the feature was disabled. CISA added the flaw to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog.

Once the patch is in, can you say what the attacker already took?

比特币的 “ 四年周期” 一直被人讨论不休。

先说观点：比特币是一种大宗商品，但叠加了科技股属性。

2025 年，不少聪明的分析师都说比特币不会跌破 8 万、不会跌破 7 万，四年周期已经失效。

但从现在的走势看，四年周期依然有效，价格正在朝着周期对应的位置修正。

甚至正在向 @wolfyxbt 狼总2025年时算的狼波周期靠拢。

我基本同意 @uxuykevin 提到的“比特币是一个类似大宗商品”的说法，想在这个基础上补充一点：比特币在大宗商品之上，还叠加了科技股属性。

一个资产是什么属性，取决于谁在持有它。

过去，持有比特币最多的是币圈自己的人。就像原油主要握在产业链上的人手里，行业内的人持有行业内的资产，这是典型的大宗商品特征。

这两年，持有美股的人和持有比特币的人，越来越是同一批人。他们通过 ETF 买比特币，既看 AI，又看加密——这一类人是“科技新贵”。比特币也就带上了科技股的属性。

这就是为什么最近比特币和美股同涨同跌。比特币 7×24 小时交易，遇到极端下跌时，这批投资者往往先卖比特币，拿钱去给美股补仓。

类似的剧本，甚至也发生在黄金身上。

黄金本来是公认的避险资产，现在却越来越多地和美股同涨同跌，反而有了风险资产的味道。

原因也一样：越来越多人买黄金，图的是收益，避险反倒成了次要的。

顺着「谁在持有」这个思路，可以推出三个有意思的结论。

一、比特币和黄金是美股的先行指标。

它们会比美股更早做出反应。当比特币和黄金同步跳水时，往往说明背后还藏着更大的流动性危机。

二、比特币抛售的终点，就是比特币回归大宗商品属性的起点

大规模抛售之后，同时重仓美股的那批投资者会逐渐离场，留下来的又是币圈原本的人，比特币重新回到大宗商品属性。

三、比特币下跌的终点，就是美股危机的起点。

当比特币和黄金的抛售达到顶点，也意味着这批投资者的流动性接近枯竭，美股真正的危机才刚开始。

一言以蔽之：
1. 这一轮，比特币可能正在经历由美股资金主导的最后一次抛售。
2. 比特币的低点，很可能对应着美股危机的起点。
3. 等到美股哀鸿遍野的时候，就是比特币走出独立复苏的时候。

牢记一句话：持有者的属性决定了资产的属性，持有者的心理决定了资产的价格。

—— 救赎之道，就在其中。

text:
As a former ‘Big Four’ auditor, I’d be concerned enough to want the evidence behind PwC’s Nvidia sign-off examined closely

PwC signed clean opinions on the accounts and financial reporting controls on 25 February 2026. Its only critical audit matter was “inventory valuation and excess purchase commitments”

Before that sign-off, Singapore had accounted for 22% of quarterly revenue by billing address. Nvidia then switched to customer-headquarters reporting, removing Singapore’s separate line

That change may be legitimate. I’d want to see how PwC established that the disclosures still fairly represented the underlying customer + export risks

Separately, the customer-funding question warrants more than a “shrug”. US audit standards explicitly tell auditors evaluating significant unusual transactions to consider whether counterparties can support the deal without the company’s financial assistance…

I’d want the investment agreements, chip orders, guarantees and side letters examined together: was funding conditional on purchases, could customers meet their obligations, and what risk or control did $NVDA retain?

No revenue “critical audit matter” doesn’t mean no revenue testing... revenue testing is a pre-requisite as becomes a key area of fraud risk but it depends whether the testing they’ve done is “sufficient”

But with an SEC accounting probe now reported, PwC’s risk assessment and the evidence supporting its “clean” opinion deserve serious scrutiny

I’d be sh*tting it if I were the NVDA PwC signing partners… buckle up buttercup I suspect they’ll apportion part of the blame for their legal team to defend if fines come their way!

text:
Ethereum is working toward making smart accounts a native part of the protocol.

And EIP-8141 is one proposal developers should watch.

Today, Ethereum accounts have two fundamentally different models:

EOAs
Controlled by private keys.
Require signatures for transactions.
Have limited native programmability.

Smart contract wallets
Support programmable authorisation.
Enable custom validation logic.
Can implement recovery and spending policies.
Often require additional infrastructure.

EIP-8141 proposes bringing native account abstraction to Ethereum through frame transactions.

Why does this matter?
Imagine wallets that natively support,
Multiple signature schemes.
Social recovery.
Sponsored gas.
Spending limits.
More flexible transaction authorization.

This also has an important long-term implication.

Ethereum needs a path toward post-quantum cryptography. Making account authorization more flexible could help wallets adopt new signature schemes without depending on today's ECDSA assumptions.

Wallets shouldn't be limited by the cryptographic and transaction models they started with.

Ethereum isn't just upgrading how transactions work. It's rethinking what an account can actually be.

text:
some thoughts about $PRL that are worth considering when thinking about investing in this.

- security budget
PRL aims to be a SoV asset, and security budget / protocol security are crucial for a SoV asset. BTC and other pure PoW networks are secured by game theory.  a potential attacker needs to burn a scarce resource (energy) to get hashrate to gain 51% control of the network. since PoW is costly and does not return any money (in itself) an attack is very expensive and not worth it economically (would be more expensive to get the 51% than what you could make by exploiting the network).

with PRL there is no such cost, the PoW (proof of work) is not "useless". their version of PoW is performing matrix multiplications that are the basis of inference. miners/providers get paid to do this by the ai customer and the PRL mined are just a byproduct / the cherry on top. they call this "duplex mining" and sell it as an upgrade to pure PoW because the work (in proof-of-work) is not wasted and is instead serving inference demand from ai customers.

this has a huge flaw.
a potential prl attacker gets most money spent on the attack back. because he gets paid for his inference work. whereas an attacker for a pure pow chain gets zero money spent on the attack back. the result is that attacking prl is much cheaper than attacking a similar sized pure pow network. pure PoW chains utilize 100% of the hash because the work is useless. whereas Pearl and other PoUW chains only utilize some small % of the hash. if we put this % at 5% (as an example) then it would be 20x cheaper to attack PRL than it would be to attack a pure PoW network of similar size / similar TAM. 

- team ethics are questionable 
they championed the claim of "no VC, no pre-mine" and simultaneously raised two funds, one for equity in the lab and one for mining PRL tokens early on. this was not properly disclosed (talked about this in my channel a couple months back, it has been leaked since). i view this as a negative. 

- potentially some cabal activity going on
multiple VCs and entities were parading around SG saying they want to buy more / double their position but it would just be so hard to source coins. from a game theory standpoint it would make zero sense to telegraph your move and allow others to frontrun yourself if you really had the intention to buy a large quantity of coins. they only possible scenario where this would make sense (from a game theory pov) is when you would be fully allocated already and want to drum up liquidity. 
another entity wrote in an article that "Pearl might actually achieve negative overhead – in other words, building kernels that are faster than the ones inference providers already use." thats straight up Fugazi, there is no world in which i believe a crypto team will produce better kernels than NVIDIA and Google. there is zero shot this becomes a reality, and if it would then it would further weaken network security as outlined in the first point of this post. just remember, these people are not your friends and they have their own agenda and motives for what they say what they say.

on the positive side:
that said, the narrative for PRL is elite. positioning itself as an AI-winner in times where most of crypto is labelled an AI-loser. it also addresses many problems of established SoVs, like quantum resistance. also maybe there is a way duplex mining can scale 20x faster than traditional PoW and therefore secure the network against malicious actors with access to compute. i have my doubts, but worth exploring this possibility.

on the "hard money / SOV" narrative i think it is currently lacking a lot. you cannot come out and label smth "money" that has not even existed 6 months before. (crypto) money properties come from the ability to not be controlled by a single entity and a decentralized network (PRL is controlled by a private company), lindy effect and having stood the test of time (PRL is a couple months old) and provable scarcity. i also think network security is most crucial in any attempt of labelling smth a store-of-value. 

curious to hear your opinions on this subject in the comments.

text:
跌麻了，大家都在哭，但我想说点不一样的。

每到熊市，大家问的都是同一个问题：这个行业是不是要完了？
可这一次，几乎没人会这么想。

因为这一轮周期，第一次回答了两个最根本的问题。

第一，比特币会不会归零？

世界已有多个国家推行国家级 BTC 战略储备；
150+ 家上市公司把 BTC 放进了资产负债表，合计持有超过 130 万枚；
美国现货 ETF 获批，持有超 125 万枚。

华尔街已经给出了答案：比特币是一种硬资产，它不是郁金香。

第二，加密能为传统金融创造什么价值？

Nasdaq 获批代币化股票、OKX-ICE 成立专为纽交所做代币化股票试点；
DTCC，美国证券市场的清算中枢，上线代币化服务，明年还要接 Solana；
链上代币化资产已超过 400 亿美元——两年前，这个数字还是几亿美元量级。

传统金融开始借用加密的基础设施，这是第一次。

这一轮周期，加密行业第一次真正走进了主流视野。

价格有周期，熊市也确实难熬。但只要这两个问题被回答，行业就回不到原点。

那么，物极必反，否极泰来，一切都会回来。

这是我对这个行业依然有底气的根本。
author: imsongshu
quoted_text:
说实话，圈内人这段时间都挺难的。

比特币不断创新低，身边的朋友一个又一个离开行业

这种感觉我太熟悉了！

想来，这已经是我在圈内经历的第四轮牛熊。

我们 2018 年开始做钱包，那年 BTC 从将近 2 万跌到 3000 多，行业冷得刺骨。

后来是 312，是 LUNA，是 FTX，每一次都比上次更像终点，

每一次都是这种感受。

八年过去，叙事换了好几轮，项目来了一批又走了一批。我们一直在做同一件事：让普通人用好链上的东西。

BitKeep 做了六年，后来被收购，成了今天的 Bitget Wallet。

@uxuycom 是第四年。

说句心里话，@uxuycom 前三年其实挺苦的，一开始完全找不准方向。很多个晚上我也问过自己，还要不要继续。

但我们一点点撑了过来，熬过了最难的时刻，现在我们已经积累到了千万级用户，有了持续稳定的现金流！

我知道接下来不会轻松，但我们愿意留下来，和大家一起，做该做的事！

每到这种时候，身边总有人问我：为什么这一次这么难熬？是不是这一次，加密行业真的要结束了？

朋友，我可以负责任地告诉你：每一次都是这样！行业还在！

我一贯的观点：比特币有类似大宗商品的属性，大宗商品的核心特点就是周期轮动。

下行的时候，各种利空接连出现，一只又一只黑天鹅跳出来，把它推向谷底；
上行的时候，利好又一个接一个，真就是 “自有大儒为我辩经” 。

而且以我的个人感受，这一轮比之前几轮熊市，已经好太多了！真的好太多了！

我不想说什么 “别人恐惧我贪婪”，这种话都是扯淡，都是风凉话。

我只想说：你现在经历的，我们经历过好几次！很难受，但都会过去！

熬过冬天，春天来时，我们一起在场！

另外，如果你刚好有时间，可以来曼谷跟我们聊聊，@uxuycom 恰巧也搭了个场子。

老朋友、新朋友都欢迎，只要你还在这个行业里。

来听听别人的故事也好，喝杯酒、跟朋友诉诉苦也好。

对 @uxuycom 有什么建议，或者有什么我们能帮上的，都欢迎来聊。

不管行业怎么变，我们都会一直在 build。

text:
$PONS ｜ 收入数据口径差很大，如果链上那组靠谱，60M可能低估了

之前两周一直觉得通缩飞轮在空转，日手续费从千万塌到十万。但这两天看到另一组链上数据，让我想修正一下。

有人扒出来平台日收入维持在百万美金级别，国库还囤了300万美金准备回购，链上市占从60%冲到80%。如果这组数据靠谱，那之前"费率塌方"的判断可能过于悲观了，或者不同时间点的数据差异真的很大。

这就有意思了。平台还活着，链上份额反而在涨，收入可能也没那么低，但币价跌了91%。这种走势通常两种可能：市场在提前定价某个还没暴露的问题，或者恐慌抛售把价格砸穿了基本面。

我偏后者，但不完全确定。偏的理由是：如果平台真的日入百万级别，80%回购销毁，年化通缩是实打实的。60M市值对这个收入水平来说偏低了。不确定的地方在于，收入能不能持续，这个取决于RH链的活跃度，不可控。

讲真之前那组"十万级别"的数据把我吓到了，导致10月到11月初过于保守，价格到了我说的区间反而犹豫了。这算是给自己上了一课：不同口径的数据差别很大，二手信息做判断容易被带偏，该去链上自己验证。

这个位置在考虑把底仓补一笔，但还在等0.085的支撑确认。

author: 0xSammy
quoted_text:
As a former ‘Big Four’ auditor, I’d be concerned enough to want the evidence behind PwC’s Nvidia sign-off examined closely

PwC signed clean opinions on the accounts and financial reporting controls on 25 February 2026. Its only critical audit matter was “inventory valuation and excess purchase commitments”

Before that sign-off, Singapore had accounted for 22% of quarterly revenue by billing address. Nvidia then switched to customer-headquarters reporting, removing Singapore’s separate line

That change may be legitimate. I’d want to see how PwC established that the disclosures still fairly represented the underlying customer + export risks

Separately, the customer-funding question warrants more than a “shrug”. US audit standards explicitly tell auditors evaluating significant unusual transactions to consider whether counterparties can support the deal without the company’s financial assistance…

I’d want the investment agreements, chip orders, guarantees and side letters examined together: was funding conditional on purchases, could customers meet their obligations, and what risk or control did $NVDA retain?

No revenue “critical audit matter” doesn’t mean no revenue testing... revenue testing is a pre-requisite as becomes a key area of fraud risk but it depends whether the testing they’ve done is “sufficient”

But with an SEC accounting probe now reported, PwC’s risk assessment and the evidence supporting its “clean” opinion deserve serious scrutiny

I’d be sh*tting it if I were the NVDA PwC signing partners… buckle up buttercup I suspect they’ll apportion part of the blame for their legal team to defend if fines come their way!

text:
NX2Apple v1.5.0 is out.
Zero IPA reinstalls for new games, a slim shared shell IPA of just a few tens of MB, multi-engine switching, minute-level rebuilds, and 574 upstream engine commits.

What is new in v1.5.0:

1. Multi-engine workbench
Switch in one click between nxnative, MacNativeGames (with MNG badges for first-party Mac play), and self-updating nxkit (Beta).

2. Minute-level fast refresh without original ROMs
Build a game once on v1.5.0 to keep persistent build seeds. Around 90% of future engine updates batch-refresh in minutes — no original ROM or huge temp folders needed.

3. Add new iOS games without reinstalling the IPA
Export a standalone DmGame.framework into Files -> NX2Apple -> Frameworks and launch right away. Import a .p12 certificate inside the iOS shell for on-device signing, or hot-push directly on iOS 27.

4. Slim shared shell IPA (just a few tens of MB)
Compiled shader trailers now live inside external .img archives, keeping the shared NX2Apple.ipa down to a few tens of megabytes for painless AltStore and SideStore signing (separate from single-game all-in-one builds).

5. Full iOS Shortcuts support + PiP guide
Pin any game directly to your iPhone or iPad Home Screen with the built-in 6-step walkthrough and floating PiP card, or automate it — connect your Bluetooth controller and auto-launch your game.

6. Major Windows build overhaul
Multi-game batch build queue, an on-demand 2 GiB emulated heap that clears large Oodle blocks like Pokemon Violet, fixed Windows/exFAT build seeds and legacy folder adoption, plus smarter Defender and VC++ diagnostics.

7. Background audio mixing
Keep Apple Music or podcasts playing right into your game cleanly with zero crackling.

8. Per-game update badges
Supported Games and hero cards now show which NX2Apple version last improved each title — 80 out of 102 tracked titles carry the "Improved in 1.5" badge so you know exactly what to refresh.

9. Redesigned Dark Glass UI & Console Mode
A crisp dark design system across the launcher, built-first library, redesigned two-column Console Mode, Switch 2 eShop banner fallbacks, and an interactive 16:9 cover cropper on iOS.

10. 574 upstream engine commits (to 9922456)
Over 140 supported titles (208 profiles in the engine tree), Fire Emblem verified at 60 FPS on iPhone at just 1.51W CPU, OOT Switch 2 edition completed through the credits on Mac, faster A15/A16 multi-core texture decoding, plus Polish and Thai support.

author: oskarth
quoted_text:
I watched all 8 episodes of The Altruists, the Netflix series about Sam Bankman-Fried, Caroline Ellison and the collapse of FTX.

Genuinely can’t believe how dirty they did CZ.

Netflix portrays CZ as someone who was jealous of FTX’s growth, stealing their developers, bribing VCs and trying to get Sam and Caroline to shut down their exchange.

(In reality, Binance was one of the earliest investors in FTX)

FTX eventually bought back Binance’s stake in 2021 for $2.1B in FTT, BNB and BUSD.

There’s a scene in episode 4 where CZ suggests that Sam should give Alameda access to FTX customer trading data so they can front-run their own users.

SBF is portrayed as the one who refuses to do something unethical.

There’s no publicly documented evidence that this conversation ever happened tho

Even Forbes questioned why Netflix included this scene.

The series makes it look like CZ had a personal vendetta against Sam and was waiting for the perfect opportunity to destroy FTX.

Keep in mind that CoinDesk published Alameda’s balance sheet on November 2, 2022.

CZ announced that Binance would liquidate its remaining FTT on November 6, citing risk management and what happened with LUNA.

Binance agreed to potentially acquire FTX on November 8 and pulled out a day later after conducting due diligence.

FTX filed for bankruptcy on November 11.

CZ didn’t create the $8.7B hole in FTX. 

His actions accelerated the collapse of a company that was already insolvent.

In July 2026, a Delaware court dismissed the FTX estate’s claims against Binance related to CZ’s tweets during the collapse, although the claims regarding the 2021 share buyback survived.

Yet Netflix decided to portray CZ as someone who never intended to save FTX and was purely interested in humiliating SBF.

I’m not saying CZ is a saint either don’t get me wrong here 

Meanwhile, millions of people had their money stuck on an exchange because its founder was using customer deposits to fund his other business.

The guy responsible for that was sentenced to 25 years in prison.

You don’t need to invent a villain when the story already has one.

5. 硬件：仅HW4，老车无缘。

本质是法规+数据合规限制，非故意减配。满血版仍待进一步审批。

➥ Project Spotlight - Week 47/2026

Here are 9 projects worth a closer look.

➢ @tokastra

Here's what they do, and what could set them apart.

…

— | Tokastra

Tokastra makes it easier to compare the same stock across Ondo, xStocks, Robinhood, Coinbase, and other platforms. Its screener brings prices, issuers, and onchain volume into one place, saving you from jumping between sites.

…

— | Laserbeam

Laserbeam lets you describe a strategy in plain English, then have an AI agent backtest it and trade around the clock. Guardrails built into the protocol limit what it can do with your funds. It's planned as a launch app on @LayerZero_Core ATLAS and isn't live yet.
…

— | Supermassive

Supermassive is a planned @Solana derivatives venue from @temporal_xyz. Apps and market makers compete for orders, while one shared onchain clearinghouse holds collateral, letting you open a position through one venue and close it through another. Perps and spot come first, with options, dated futures, and prediction markets planned after.

…

— | Creddit

Creddit is a credit analytics, it helps you look beyond headline APYs. Its onchain fixed-income terminal covers repo lending, carry and looping strategies, and money-market-style funds, showing actual yield against SOFR, a US dollar benchmark rate, alongside utilization and collateral risk.

…

— | Leaps Finance

Leaps is a Solana options protocol where you earn upfront premiums by selling (not buying) options. Deposit SOL/cbBTC to sell covered calls, or USDC to sell cash-secured puts. Market makers bid via an onchain auction and the premium hits your wallet immediately; at expiry you either sell/buy at the strike or get your collateral back. Positions can’t be closed early.

…

— | Street

Street is building a market for private-company shares with sales approved by the companies themselves. You get direct ownership without SPV fund layers or carry fees. Access is opening to selected accredited investors and funds.

…

— | Derpetual

Derpetual offers "abstract futures": leveraged bets on almost any number, with longs and shorts settling directly against each other without an order book or market maker. Its partner app Derp is live on memecoins and reports over $4M in volume, and one founder is a @thielfellowship.

…

— | SmartX

SmartX brings social posts and onchain trading into one app. Trader profiles show real positions and profit and loss, and you can trade straight from a post in one tap, with fiat funding available too. It's in closed beta with zero trading fees during the beta, and says it's backed by @yzilabs.
…

— | CRSHMARKET

CRSHMARKET turns livestream moments into quick yes/no prediction markets on @monad, from esports to IRL streams. It announced a $3.5M seed round that included Reciprocal Ventures and reports 80K users and $20M in volume, both team-reported figures.

🚨 @Chainflip - Loss $4.86M (2026-11-21)

Network: Ethereum

Type: Private Key Compromise (aggregate/TSS signing key)

The Chainflip Vault was swept of its entire liquid balance — 520.2 ETH, 3.25M USDC and 758K USDT (~$4.86M) — to a fresh single-tx EOA (0x7d14…1eaf). The drain went through Vault.transferBatch, gated by KeyManager.consumeKeyNonce, whose Schnorr signature verified against the live on-chain aggregate key. Epoch rotation (setAggKeyWithAggKey) was normal and last occurred ~2.4 days earlier, so this was a valid signature from the real aggregate/TSS key authorizing an arbitrary full-vault egress to an attacker address — consistent with a compromise of the validator network's aggregate signing key rather than a signature-verification bug. Relayer/sender (0x78fa…2db0) is a brand-new EOA whose only tx is this drain; the recipient was seeded by a laundering cluster routing into Uniswap.

text: SITUATION UPDATED: The Riemann Hypothesis proof has passed the independent kernel check. MIT's Andrew Sutherland exported Alpöge and Claude's full proof and ran it through separately written kernels. nanoda (Rust) accepted it in about 28 minutes. con-leche accepted all 1.47 million declarations and confirmed the five theorems, including RH itself, match Mathlib-only statements. lean4lean passed all 175,187 modules, and Lean's own kernel replay passed with zero rejections. A Lean bug is now essentially ruled out, since every checker would have to share it. Two slower checks are still running, and nothing has failed. What's left is the human part: no readable proof exists yet, and the Clay prize needs publication plus two years of review. The Riemann Hypothesis is proven, but not yet understood.
author: haojun222
quoted_text: SITUATION DETECTED: The Riemann Hypothesis proof was verified overnight. MIT's Andrew Sutherland and others independently compiled Levent Alpöge and Claude's Lean code, about 17 million lines across 175,000 files, and the Lean kernel accepted it using only the three standard axioms. I went through the code myself: the final theorem uses Mathlib's own definition of RiemannHypothesis, nothing in the project redefines it, there's no sorry and no custom axioms. text:
45 天，美股蒸发 6 万亿美元。AI 泡沫真的破了吗？

Kobeissi Letter 一篇长文刷屏 X，阅读量突破 1000 万。文章给出了一个与当前市场悲观情绪截然不同的判断：AI 泡沫没有破裂，市场可能正在酝酿新一轮机会。

从 10 月 6 日标普 500 创下新高至今，美股连续 31 个交易日平均每天蒸发约 2250 亿美元。伊朗战争、中期选举、英伟达风波、AI 资本开支争议接连冲击市场，资金在流动性紧张时争相撤离。

但另一面的数据却很有意思：

标普 500 三季度 EPS 同比增长 31.9%，创至少四年来最强表现，企业盈利已连续 13 个季度超预期。英伟达远期市盈率更是降至约 9 倍。

股价在崩，盈利却在增长。

Kobeissi Letter 认为，即使标普再跌 10%，仍属于健康回调。真正决定 AI 叙事能否延续的，是 2027 年上半年科技巨头的资本开支能否兑现为实际回报。

他们并不急于宣布市场见底，但也提醒投资者，不要把「还会再跌 30%」当成必然结局。

2025 年 4 月，恐慌过后资金迅速回流科技股。这一次会不会重演？

问题或许已经从「AI 是不是泡沫」，变成了「哪些 AI 公司值得在恐慌中买入」。

在一波大跌的过程中应该加仓

但是更聪明的做法是看到止跌信号后再加仓

那怎么判断市场是否止跌呢？

我从下面这几个角度带大家一起分析下

1. 如果盘中有大跌，要看当天能否收回来，如果收回来并留下较长下影线。这只是初步判断的信号

2. 随后几天不再明显创新低。再次下探时，跌幅变小、成交缩小；短暂跌破后能迅速收回

3.先反弹，随后回落不破前低，再涨过第一轮反弹高点，这是更可靠的止跌确认

4. 不只是少数大股票撑指数，多数股票跟涨，VIX 恐慌指数也持续回落，最少要回落到20以下，如果能有两三个指标出现，判断止跌的可信度更高。

所以你们学会了吗？下次还会在下跌的时候接飞刀吗？

text:
反思一下。

1. 没有把 Ai 和半导体的下跌太当回事。

实际上这一波的下跌主要动力仍然是美国和伊朗战争导致的油价上涨，但韩国的杠杆ETF已经提醒了，明明已经看到了，而且自己都在做空。却没有多思考对美股的影响。

在之前就已经知道了 AI 的资本开支过高，但觉得 AI 仍然是刚需，知道了美国半导体也加了不少杠杆，更知道了通胀压力很大，却没有谨慎。

结果就是半导体持续下跌导致了 Bitcoin 也跌跌不休。

2. 对于美联储过于理想化。

9月坚信不加息其实就应该悔悟了，结果始终觉得大家都知道是油价的原因导致的通胀上涨。所以应该不会太激进，而且过于理想在于认为货币政策也未必能太大的影响 AI 的进展，但加息 50 确实是有点吓人了。

3. 对于川普还有幻想。

川普在任上已经快一半的时间了，经常是看到情况不对就 TACO ，即便是这次对伊朗也是经常 TACO，结果没想到这次竟然硬了这么久，尤其是在伊朗已经相对认怂的时候还会这么硬。

虽然川普的反复在做空石油上有些盈利，但导致通胀上涨从而影响大的仓位就是过于对短期小仓位的执着而忽视了大仓位。

4. 注意力过于分散。

从开始用 AI 以后写了很多 AI 的东西，每天玩的不亦乐乎，上周虽然已经反应过来了，停了多数AI 的充值，但想着钱花都花了，最后额度也不能浪费，就还在继续写些有的没的的应用，分散了大量的时间。

然后就是石油，合约，双币，期权，现货什么都做了一点，最搞笑的是，我竟然完全忘记了我还有一单 62,000 美元的多单，对，就是完全忘记了，因为最近一直做期权，打开的都是期权，就完全忘记了还有一个合约在。

5. 对于中期选举过于乐观。

即便是现在。我还是觉得中期以后应该有反弹的机会，这个机会主要就来自于民主党掌握两院以后推定美国和伊朗的停火，战争结束，霍尔木兹开放，油价下降，通胀降低，美联储恢复宽松，流动性上涨，投资偏好提高，这些都不是大概率，而是会必然发生的事情。

但时间却未必如我想的这么连贯，其中最应该反省的就是把未来会发生的事件想象的一帆风顺，而实际上虽然目的地却是是没错的，但中间的过程可能很坎坷。

6. 展望一下近期未来。

如果半导体和AI 没有反弹，那么 $BTC 很大概率会还继续下跌，跌倒一个大家都觉得便宜的价格，这个价格可以通过现货 ETF 的买卖情况来确定。

即便是 BTC 的价格下跌，但只要购买力在逐渐提升，就可能是反弹的机会，这种判断方式的准确率还是挺高的，而当 ETF 的资金都开始卖的时候，就一定要小心。

IBIT的大规模资金变动可能才是最值得关注的“聪明钱”。

text:
Over the last few days, many residents and RWAs have reached out to me asking one question: 

How can stray dogs be removed from private residential societies when municipal authorities refuse to act, claiming it is against the rules?

Many are also facing intimidation and threats from those opposing any action.

In the interest of everyone, I am putting together the legal position and the steps residents can take.

This is not an illegal demand. We are asking for lawful action, enforcement of the law and the safety of residents, children and senior citizens.

Please read, share and join this effort in numbers. Write to your municipal authorities. Demand answers. Make your voices heard before the Government and the Courts.

A lawful demand for human safety is not unlawful. Don't be intimidated.

==========================
1/6 — THE RULE EVERYONE KEEPS CITING

The provision repeatedly invoked to oppose removal of stray dogs is Rule 11(19) of the Animal Birth Control Rules, 2023.

It reads:

“(19) The dogs shall be released at the same place or locality from where they were captured and the date, time and place of their release shall be recorded after their complete recovery and the representative of the local authority or of the animal welfare organisation shall accompany the team at the time of release and from time to time, the Board may provide a suitable application for geo-tagging the location of the dogs during capture and release.”

This is the provision being invoked to resist action in residential premises. But it cannot be read in isolation.

text:
比特币的 “ 四年周期” 一直被人讨论不休。

先说观点：比特币是一种大宗商品，但叠加了科技股属性。

2025 年，不少聪明的分析师都说比特币不会跌破 8 万、不会跌破 7 万，四年周期已经失效。

但从现在的走势看，四年周期依然有效，价格正在朝着周期对应的位置修正。

甚至正在向 @wolfyxbt 狼总2025年时算的狼波周期靠拢。

我基本同意 @uxuykevin 提到的“比特币是一个类似大宗商品”的说法，想在这个基础上补充一点：比特币在大宗商品之上，还叠加了科技股属性。

一个资产是什么属性，取决于谁在持有它。

过去，持有比特币最多的是币圈自己的人。就像原油主要握在产业链上的人手里，行业内的人持有行业内的资产，这是典型的大宗商品特征。

这两年，持有美股的人和持有比特币的人，越来越是同一批人。他们通过 ETF 买比特币，既看 AI，又看加密——这一类人是“科技新贵”。比特币也就带上了科技股的属性。

这就是为什么最近比特币和美股同涨同跌。比特币 7×24 小时交易，遇到极端下跌时，这批投资者往往先卖比特币，拿钱去给美股补仓。

类似的剧本，甚至也发生在黄金身上。

黄金本来是公认的避险资产，现在却越来越多地和美股同涨同跌，反而有了风险资产的味道。

原因也一样：越来越多人买黄金，图的是收益，避险反倒成了次要的。

顺着「谁在持有」这个思路，可以推出三个有意思的结论。

一、比特币和黄金是美股的先行指标。

它们会比美股更早做出反应。当比特币和黄金同步跳水时，往往说明背后还藏着更大的流动性危机。

二、比特币抛售的终点，就是比特币回归大宗商品属性的起点

大规模抛售之后，同时重仓美股的那批投资者会逐渐离场，留下来的又是币圈原本的人，比特币重新回到大宗商品属性。

三、比特币下跌的终点，就是美股危机的起点。

当比特币和黄金的抛售达到顶点，也意味着这批投资者的流动性接近枯竭，美股真正的危机才刚开始。

一言以蔽之：
1. 这一轮，比特币可能正在经历由美股资金主导的最后一次抛售。
2. 比特币的低点，很可能对应着美股危机的起点。
3. 等到美股哀鸿遍野的时候，就是比特币走出独立复苏的时候。

牢记一句话：持有者的属性决定了资产的属性，持有者的心理决定了资产的价格。

—— 救赎之道，就在其中。

quoted_text:
说实话，圈内人这段时间都挺难的。

比特币不断创新低，身边的朋友一个又一个离开行业

这种感觉我太熟悉了！

想来，这已经是我在圈内经历的第四轮牛熊。

我们 2018 年开始做钱包，那年 BTC 从将近 2 万跌到 3000 多，行业冷得刺骨。

后来是 312，是 LUNA，是 FTX，每一次都比上次更像终点，

每一次都是这种感受。

八年过去，叙事换了好几轮，项目来了一批又走了一批。我们一直在做同一件事：让普通人用好链上的东西。

BitKeep 做了六年，后来被收购，成了今天的 Bitget Wallet。

@uxuycom 是第四年。

说句心里话，@uxuycom 前三年其实挺苦的，一开始完全找不准方向。很多个晚上我也问过自己，还要不要继续。

但我们一点点撑了过来，熬过了最难的时刻，现在我们已经积累到了千万级用户，有了持续稳定的现金流！

我知道接下来不会轻松，但我们愿意留下来，和大家一起，做该做的事！

每到这种时候，身边总有人问我：为什么这一次这么难熬？是不是这一次，加密行业真的要结束了？

朋友，我可以负责任地告诉你：每一次都是这样！行业还在！

我一贯的观点：比特币有类似大宗商品的属性，大宗商品的核心特点就是周期轮动。

下行的时候，各种利空接连出现，一只又一只黑天鹅跳出来，把它推向谷底；
上行的时候，利好又一个接一个，真就是 “自有大儒为我辩经” 。

而且以我的个人感受，这一轮比之前几轮熊市，已经好太多了！真的好太多了！

我不想说什么 “别人恐惧我贪婪”，这种话都是扯淡，都是风凉话。

我只想说：你现在经历的，我们经历过好几次！很难受，但都会过去！

熬过冬天，春天来时，我们一起在场！

另外，如果你刚好有时间，可以来曼谷跟我们聊聊，@uxuycom 恰巧也搭了个场子。

老朋友、新朋友都欢迎，只要你还在这个行业里。

来听听别人的故事也好，喝杯酒、跟朋友诉诉苦也好。

对 @uxuycom 有什么建议，或者有什么我们能帮上的，都欢迎来聊。

不管行业怎么变，我们都会一直在 build。

相比于AI解决了黎曼猜想，有人在四个月前就预言了这件事令我感到十分地震惊。而且发生的时间节点完全准确。这仿佛充斥着德尔斐神谕一般的留白。

原帖说，AI会跨越黎曼猜想、P=NP等人类百年未解的数学难题，接着颠覆停机问题和哥德尔不完备定理，人类认知和逻辑的极限被彻底打破，最后突破物理与算力限制，让Fable 7能直接运行在每个人的手机上。
原帖说，Fable 6 证明 P=NP 时，内容完全无法理解，人类看了不知所云，但所有AI模型，都为之疯狂。按照这个逻辑递进，AI 算力突破极限并在手机端普及后，这很可能是一种超越人类感官与大脑承受极限的音频或信息序列，我想是类似科幻作品中的模因危害的不可名状之物。它一经播放就改写了人类的意识、引发了全球性的集体顿悟或疯狂，甚至直接终结了旧世界。

至少它已经正确了一次。按照它的最终预言，人类文明的命运会在2027年2月14日这一天被彻底改写。拭目以待。

February 10th we get proof that scale is a spatial dimension, that holographic encoding drops the memory cost of training and inference by so much that fable 7 can run natively on your phone.

text:
这篇论文《Language Model Harnesses Can Be Compositional Generalizers》非常值得一读。harness的作用还是非常大的。 

传统 harness 把完整历史塞进 prompt（trajectory-as-a-prompt），容易导致 上下文腐烂。论文主张好的 harness（如 RLM、CodeAct 等）应通过程序化分解、上下文卸载和子调用，让每一个单独的 LLM 调用看到的内容都尽量保持“局部 in-distribution”。这样即使整体任务很长或很新，单个调用仍落在模型已熟悉的分布内，从而实现组合泛化。 

论文里用一个RLM harness来实验： 
超长输入（文档、任务描述等）不直接塞进模型的上下文，而是存成一个 Python 变量，放在外部的 REPL 环境（可交互的代码执行环境）里。主模型只看到很短的历史，它自己之前写的代码 + 代码执行结果的简要信息。 主模型的工作是写 Python 代码来操作这个变量（超长输入）， 

-例如：切片、检索、过滤长文档； 
-把内容分成多个 chunk； 
-调用子模型（llm_query() 之类的函数）去处理每个小 chunk； 
-把子模型的结果存回变量，再继续汇总。 
-子调用可以再递归（子模型也可以用同样的方式再拆）。

最终主模型输出最终答案（通常通过设置某个 FINAL 变量或特殊终止信号）。 这样主模型每次看到的上下文都很短且结构相似，子模型处理的都是小块。 

另外可以通过两种训练方式来训练主模型的拆解策略能力：
 1）短任务拆解训练得到更长任务的拆解能力 
-只给它短版本的任务做训练（比如 32K token 的文档）。 
-主模型不断尝试写出不同的拆解代码，执行后看最终任务是否做对。 
-用 GRPO 等 RL 算法根据奖励更新主模型参数。 
-训练一段时间后，它会发现一些稳定的拆解套路（比如“按固定长度切分 → 每个块单独总结 → 再合并”）。 
-这些套路因为和具体长度无关，所以直接迁移到更长的任务（256K、甚至百万级）时仍然有效。 

2）Surrogate Harness Training ，是为了解决一个很实际的问题：对于特别长、跑一遍成本极高的任务。 

-用更强的模型（如 Claude）生成大量合成短任务； 
-在这些合成环境里用假的工具调用和假的子模型回答； 
-只训练主模型的“调度行为”（怎么写拆解代码、怎么调用、怎么汇总）； 
-训练完后，再把这个主模型放到真实的长任务环境里使用。 
-实验显示这种方式比直接在真实长任务上做 RL 更高效，性能还有明显提升。 

实验表明，只在短任务上用 RL 训练 RLM，就能泛化到 2–64 倍更长的任务；在一个领域训练也能迁移到共享潜在分解结构的其他领域。同等训练提升下，评估提升远好于直接训练基础 Transformer（有时接近 10 倍 eval lift）。这把泛化负担从“模型自己硬泛化”转移到了 harness 的分解策略上。
author: alacheng
quoted_text:
Harnesses used to be a crutch for weak LLMs. In 2026 and onward, with stronger models, harnesses now offer a mechanism for composing an LLM’s existing and new capabilities to generalize well beyond their training environments.

In our new paper, LM Harnesses are Compositional Generalizers, we explore how various harness abstractions enable LM systems to generalize over task length, task strategies, recursive task depth, and more through composing existing LLM capabilities. These abstractions provide a means for more data-efficient training, especially over long tasks, by keeping trajectories locally in-distribution (LID) — i.e., shaping all individual LLM calls to be in-distribution.

For tasks that take a very long time to roll out, this implies that we can even perform surrogate harness training, meaning we train an individual LLM call instead of doing the very long harness rollout, using purely synthetic tasks, with fake tool calls + sub-agents!

A common idea floating around is that LLMs will absorb harnesses and make them obsolete. We disagree, and argue that we haven’t sufficiently explored what harnesses can provide.

The full paper, logs, codebase, and data are available: https://t.co/AXBjdoqmiz

The law of the universe is simple and has never been updated:
The strong feed on the weak.
Everything else is noise.
Nature doesn’t debate it. The lion doesn’t negotiate with the gazelle. The shark doesn’t ask the smaller fish for consent. The wolf doesn’t lose sleep over the sheep’s feelings. They simply take. 
Humans are no different. We just added language, laws, and stories to hide the same equation.
The weak are not saved by fairness, slogans, or morality. They are consumed by whoever arrives with actual leverage:
1. Those who hold political power write the rules everyone else must follow
2. Those who control money decide who eats and who starves
3. Those with sharper ideas move while others are still talking
4. Those favored by luck walk through doors that effort alone never opens
5. Those who harvest public sympathy become untouchable
6. Those who own influence decide which version of reality is allowed
7. Those who master manipulation make the weak volunteer for their own defeat
8. Those with pure nerve simply take what the hesitant are too afraid to defend

This is not cruelty.
This is the oldest pattern in existence.
Ouer universe does not reward the kind.
It rewards the capable.
The rest is just the sound of the weak explaining why they lost.

quoted_text:
🚨 A domain controller can stay online while its database is stolen. A wallet’s private key can stay on the device while the money moves out.

In the November 21 edition of GCSA Insights, we break down five incidents that show how much damage follows when trusted systems are turned against their users.

1. VMware vCenter — Domain controller database stolen
ARMORY CASTLE exploited a vCenter zero-day to gain administrative access, reached an ESXi host, and extracted the Active Directory database from a virtual disk.

2. Wagyu XMR1 — 13.51 million USDC cashed out
The attacker moved 5.2 million XMR1 and sold 369,623 tokens on Hyperliquid. XMR1 fell from roughly $500 to $1.

3. Fluidkey — At least $1.58 million traced across six chains
Fluidkey says a third-party logging tool exposed session data. Unauthorized transactions were signed when users opened the app, then broadcast through Fluidkey’s own relayer. The private keys stayed on users’ devices.

4. Cisco Expressway — Four cluster nodes compromised
An intrusion at a Russian company spread from two internet-facing appliances to two internal nodes in the same cluster.

5. Apache Roller — The off switch came too late
Affected versions processed XML-RPC requests before checking whether the feature was disabled. CISA added the flaw to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog.

Once the patch is in, can you say what the attacker already took?

土豆姐 Lauren 用 AI 的这个小习惯大家可以学习一下。

她在 pstack 里有个很喜欢的 Skill，名字就叫「用你自己的话说」。

每次给 Agent 布置任务，她会先交代背景，再让它用自己的话复述一遍，确认它到底有没有理解自己的意图。

这个动作看着简单，却能拦住很多返工。你说“优化一下”，它可能已经准备重做整个页面；你只想改几个字，它连布局都替你安排好了。

像装修开工前先对一遍图纸，师傅手艺再好，也得先确认两个人想法是否一致。

Lauren 想表达的意思就是：Agent 已经很能干了，理解需求和意图正在成为瓶颈。

AI 执行得越快，开工前这次确实就越重要。花一分钟确认方向，往往能省掉后面一大串“不是这个意思”，节省后续大量时间和精力。 https://t.co/B24WsJa4aB

text:
卧槽，兄弟们，太爆炸了

替黄仁勋喊冤的人，跑到丹麦国家电视台去了。

这人叫 DHH，丹麦程序员，Ruby on Rails 的作者，做 Basecamp、HEY 的 37signals 的 CTO，X 上 96 万粉。

黄仁勋因为婚外情等一连串的事下了台，英伟达董事会前几天又没同意让他回来，他上了丹麦国家电视台 DR 的《Deadline》，开口第一句就是：我们需要黄仁勋回到掌舵的位置。

视频里说的是丹麦语，大意是这样：

黄仁勋把人生最后 33 年都花在建这家公司上，它成了世界上最值钱的公司，就是因为他把它建起来了。英伟达身上所有的权力，都是他自己造出来的，不是从谁手里拿来的，这东西以前根本不存在。

主持人追问：这么大的价值，全系在一个人身上，这本身不也是巨大的风险吗？

他直接顶回去：这是前提。没有他，这些价值压根不会存在。

更狠的是最后几句。世界历史上，从来没有哪家科技公司是靠一个委员会走到英伟达今天这个位置的，从来都是一个个有激情的人造出来的，不是那些体面的官僚。下一个英伟达，不会从布鲁塞尔出来。

发视频的时候他还补了一刀：欧洲很多人总担心科技权力，好像黄仁勋是从别人手里偷来的。不是，那是他在英伟达干了 33 年，一点点干出来的。

前两天马斯克在纽约时报 DealBook 峰会上也说，黄仁勋不可替代。

这就像一支球队，靠一个主教练从低级别联赛一路打进欧冠决赛，后来因为场外的事把他换了，俱乐部说以后由一个技术委员会带队。

委员会能把账管好，可没听说哪个委员会带队拿过冠军。

欧洲这些年最拿手的，是给科技巨头立规矩、开罚单。DHH 这番话骂的不只是英伟达董事会：你们最怕的那种权力，恰恰是你们自己造不出来的东西。 https://t.co/KLKU82bo0u

text:
How vol funds die, and how Alpha Strategies (our flagship) is built not to

LMR’s flagship lost 24% in March 2020 on a trade its own risk chief later said the firm could not price or stress test properly. Up to then it had 19 losing months out of 119. Same month, the book our PM ran at a multi-billion Asia fund printed +10.24% (SS&C-audited).

The trade was long Asian vol against short US vol through OTC cross-corridor variance swaps, and it was valued off bank month-end marks that went to extremes when Malachite failed. That is LMR’s own CRO talking, years later. LMR Long Horizon was in our benchmark back then and seemed a genius for a couple of years before us. Bloomberg reported on 26 March 2020 that it was being wound down after its bets on volatility backfired. The flagship went to its investors for capital and finished the year down about 6%.

We have seen this a few times now. A not liquid second or third order effect seems smart to the investors, then gets carried away irrespective of timing. Listed or OTC, does not matter. Credit Suisse held a $7M exposure limit against Malachite and lost $214M. AIMCo’s 95% VaR showed minimal risk on a variance book that went on to lose C$2.1B. LJM was all listed S&P options and still went down over 80% in two days in 2018 once the clearing broker called. QVR made 78% in 2020, and the successor fund is closing this year after losing 30% (redemptions, no margin call that we can find). To be fair we picked these because they failed, and nobody outside LMR has seen Long Horizon’s book.

Volatility trading is actually less about modelling and more a funding and relationship business than many think. The Fed looked at March 2020 and found the larger dealers supplied disproportionately more of the funding, and that funds with longer share restrictions cut their positions less.

So that is what we built Alpha Strategies around. We would rather take liquid delta than an illiquid third order effect, even if sounds less smart. The mandate runs from -20% to +200% of NAV in delta, mostly perps and listed options with a screen price. Capital is locked for the epoch and comes back to the vault at settlement, which means we cannot be redeemed out of a trade halfway through.

We do trade the exotic stuff, in small size and fully funded. Our IBIT/EWY Corridor vault ran a realized-vol swap with the worst case written into the payoff and fixings off official closes. Alpha Strategies took the other side at under 1% of its NAV. KOSPI 200 fell 18% in three sessions a week after launch, and vault depositors still netted 16.7% over the 64 days.

The record so far is 33 epochs since December 2023, 32 of them positive. That compounds to +216% net at a Sharpe of about 2.5 (our numbers, every settlement is on-chain). In February 2025 ETH fell 33% and the vaults closed positive. Worst drawdown inside an epoch was 3% to 4% back in 2024, about 1% since.

Fees are 0% management and 20% of an epoch’s profit, nothing on a losing one. BVI-regulated investment manager, Anchorage custody, contracts audited by Paladin and Cyfrin. We think capacity is about $200M with the TradFi sleeve. The current epoch closes 15 January 2027 and the next window opens then, by vault or SMA. DMs are open if you want to do due diligence.

We do not think we are better modellers than the people above, several of them were better. What we know is that we can get out. When we are wrong it is in a size we can fund, mostly in something with a price on a screen.

Fade D2 at your own risk.

几年前，听说一个反撸的 L2 项目，给 KOL 每人发几万U 的茶水费，我当时大为震撼，就去扒了链上 Tx，开始对这个行业祛魅

顺便聊下转账记录这事，链上真没隐私，收款人就是裸奔。正常收付款，不想主动公开账本，American Fortress （美国堡垒）就是想解决这个需求

🌈美国团队，美国公司，美国专利

先说下 @Americanfort_io 背景，不是华人项目，它背后的公司是 MatterFi Inc.，注册在美国怀俄明州（彭博的企业身份记录里能查到）

创始人 Michal “Mehow” Pospieszalski，毕业于弗吉尼亚大学计算机系，创业做了 8 年的 Rune Wallet 钱包基建被 MatterFi 收购

我翻到一张他 2018 年出席 CIS 大会的照片，履历看，确实是旧金山湾区科技圈子的人

他的研究方向是钱包安全，项目有专利保护，2025 年拿到了美国国家专利

🔹我个人觉得，这种实名且有美国专利的项目，比币圈某些圈钱 PPT 好很多

--

🍀项目在做什么

按官方设计，你注册一个 FortressName，比如 sam，别人在钱包里输入名字，就能转账，不用每次复制那串长地址

但它不只是给钱包起个昵称，背后会按收发对象使用独立地址，让外人更难把这个名字、收款记录和常用钱包关联起来，不是看到名字，就能顺藤摸瓜翻你的账

这项目还没发币，估计快 TGE 了，代码是$AF，看后面能上哪些交易所

保护隐私，但绝不是混币器

--

🪂 对我们有什么用？

朋友之间转 U、给客户收服务费、做线上生意，我觉得这类需求很实在。我们要的是收钱方便，不是每次收款，都顺便把常用钱包交给别人研究

项目方今年 5 月在 Arb 上推出了测试版，已经可以进行产品测试

✅ 我不知会不会有空投。。。。这个真不知道。。。

现在的项目不需要撸毛人做数据了，能解决需求的才有市场，比如 HYPE 是交易赌场，这个美国堡垒如果能把转账隐私做到位，也能成长为细分领域的一棵小树

quoted_text:
it's not that ive given up on crypto, it's just that the reason i was so fascinated with it in the past doesn't feel as true anymore

or maybe it's just been fulfilled

when i first learned about bitcoin and ethereum, i felt so against the trend

against the crowd

everyone thought i was crazy when i tried explaining why i believed this was a part of the future, and everyone said "no way"

decentralization, full sovereignty, ownership over our money, and only 21 million bitcoins ever to exist

what if one day it was adopted by governments? what if we could transact privately, without asking for permission, and have full control over our own futures?

this is what excited me

and that ethos stayed true for many years, until slowly, everything we had been manifesting started becoming reality

governments started embracing it, institutions came in, and the rest of the world finally started paying attention

but the grass is always greener on the other side

the wizard of oz was revealed

we finally got to see what was behind the curtain, and it was still really cool technology that could do a lot of amazing things

but that was it

the more crypto became a part of the world, the more it started to look like the very world we were trying to change

the same institutions, the same power structures, the same incentives, just with new technology underneath it, a new "game" if you will, just rewrapped

and i think somewhere along the way, we started confusing adoption with actually achieving what we set out to do

we spent so many years trying to convince the world that crypto was the future, that when the world finally started agreeing with us, we forgot to ask ourselves what kind of future we were actually building

don't get me wrong, i still believe in the technology, in the ability to completely change your life, and i know there are people out there building things that can genuinely change the world

but i think what i fell in love with wasn't just the technology

it was being a part of a world where we were all building something different, a left curve, retard maxer

something that would give the average person more freedom, more ownership, and more control over their own life

and of course, a "fast" way to level up the amount of gold coins you have access to, to then give you freedom to explore different pastures

which, let's be real, is what most people eventually came here for

i can't even pretend that wasn't a huge part of it for me too

but i think that's what ive been missing

not the prices, not the excitement, not even the opportunities to make money

just that feeling that we were all building towards something bigger than ourselves

or maybe what i miss is just being early, when nobody believed in any of this, and we were all figuring it out together

i don't really know

because when i look at crypto today, a lot of what we dreamed about actually happened

bitcoin is taken seriously, governments are paying attention, and institutions are putting real money behind it

i mean even from a price standpoint, it's trading as a glorified tech stock

but did any of that actually give the average person more freedom? more ownership? more control over their future?

in some ways, absolutely

in others, i think we still have a long way to go

i don't think crypto has failed, far from it

i just think we spent so much time trying to prove to the world that we were right, that somewhere along the way, we forgot why we wanted to be right in the first place

text:
Everyone is saying the S&P 500 is getting cheap on P/E. I’m not so sure.

The biggest companies in the index are almost all buying AI chips, and the main seller, Nvidia, sits in the same index. When Microsoft or Meta pays Nvidia $100, Nvidia books most of that as profit right away. The buyer spreads the cost over 5–6 years of depreciation. So the index shows a big profit today on spending that hasn’t proven it pays back yet.

And the faster capex grows, the bigger this gap gets, because depreciation always lags. Strong earnings growth during a capex boom is partly just the boom showing up in the numbers. When spending flattens, depreciation catches up with the buyers while Nvidia’s growth slows. Earnings get hit from both sides.

The real tell is cash. Big Tech earnings are at records while free cash flow is heading toward negative. When profits go up and cash goes down, the accounting is running ahead of the economics.

AI can be real and the S&P can still be more expensive than it looks. Both can be true.

text:
A smart contract can be secure today and still become incompatible with tomorrow's Ethereum upgrade.

That's one of the biggest lessons from Glamsterdam.

Two proposals are forcing developers to rethink assumptions they've relied on for years.

EIP-8037: Changes the cost of creating permanent on-chain state.
EIP-8038: Reprices state-access operations to better reflect their actual resource costs.

Why should Solidity developers care?
Some contracts rely on fixed gas assumptions, particularly around contract creation and execution.
When those assumptions change, transactions can run out of gas and fail.
This is not necessarily a Solidity compiler issue. It's a compatibility problem between deployed code and evolving protocol economics.

The Ethereum Foundation has called on developers and auditors to review affected invariants.

The takeaway for smart contract engineers:
Don't hardcode assumptions about gas costs.
Review gasleft()-dependent execution paths.
Test against proposed protocol changes.
Audit contract creation and state-access assumptions.
Don't assume immutable contracts are automatically future-proof.

Ethereum is evolving, and deployed contracts have to survive that evolution.

Writing smart contracts is one challenge. Writing contracts that survive protocol upgrades is another level of engineering.

Admiral Bobby Ray Inman passed away this week at 95.

I first met Bobby in 1987, when he and George Kozmetsky joined the Dell board together. I was 22, and the company was three years old and not yet public. Bobby had already been a four-star admiral, director of the NSA and deputy director of the CIA. Having the two of them at the table in those early days made us a better company.

Bobby served on our board until late 1993. In those years Dell grew from about $160 million in sales to nearly $3 billion.

He gave more than three decades to the Navy and the country, then came home to Texas and helped make Austin a technology center.

In April we celebrated his 95th birthday. I am grateful for that day, and for nearly 40 years of friendship.

My condolences to the Inman family.

What this video doesn't show you is the conversation that led up to it, which is basically the psyop here.

They were discussing AI agents, how individuals can delegate tasks to them, and the challenges of doing that at an enterprise level.

Jensen was trying to get the audience to understand the significance of Arthur's point. That's why he kept joking about his baud rate, comprehension, and reinforcement learning.

Now a little about this term, baud rate, it's literally a measure of how fast information is transmitted. Jensen was joking that Arthur's brain was transmitting information faster than the audience could process it. 

In other words, he was calling Arthur so intellectually advanced that the rest of the room couldn't keep up. 

Somehow, people managed to interpret that as an insult to Arthur's intelligence.

He was deliberately drawing attention to the gap between intelligence, communication, and comprehension.

Cut out the context, and suddenly Jensen looks like he's humiliating Arthur instead of emphasizing the importance of what Arthur was explaining.

When you try to use this form of manipulation, that tells me you fear him, and that your only way of destroying him is by manipulating the world with bullshit taken out of context.

I find that to be the lowest form of intelligence.

Also, to whoever follows the person who shared this, I genuinely wonder why would you follow someone who is actively deceiving you?

世界文学史上的一颗璀璨的明珠：

author: Goupenguin
quoted_text:
这个事情现在已经不是钱的问题了，是小企鹅把整个金融系统的生殖周期给打乱了。

你们知道小企鹅为什么要发明久留美飞机杯吗？我跟你讲，这个东西最早根本不是给人用的，是给比特币矿机配种的。因为比特币每四年减半一次，矿机长期没有生育能力，算力就会出现遗传性衰退。

当时日本有个研究所，专门研究显卡的卵巢功能，后来被腾讯收购了，收购的时候还送了两吨北海道的海带。

问题就出在这个海带上。

海带属于海洋生物，海洋生物没有户口，不能参与数字人民币结算。小企鹅为了绕过这个问题，就把久留美飞机杯接入了 BTC 的主网。

结果一接进去，比特币怀孕了。

但是比特币是去中心化的，怀孕之后根本找不到孩子的父亲，全球几百万台矿机都不承认这个孩子是自己的。最后只能去找马化腾做亲子鉴定。

这一下就出事了。

马化腾本来就是企鹅系的，你让企鹅去给比特币做亲子鉴定，这不是乱伦吗？所以马化腾出轨了。

他这一出轨，腾讯的股权结构就出现了染色体异常，直接传染到纳斯达克。纳斯达克当时已经怀孕三个月了，结果美联储突然宣布不降息，美股当场流产！

美股一流产，BTC 就崩盘了。整个华尔街的基金经理连夜跑去医院捐精，但是已经来不及了，因为英伟达的显卡全被小企鹅拿去做久留美飞机杯了。

现在整个金融市场生灵涂炭，几千万人的退休金变成了北海道海带，巴菲特已经连续三天没有下蛋了。

我也很难过，我昨天晚上开心的睡不着觉，因为我系统让我提前做空了全世界，我做空啦我做空啦，我太赚钱了，我买了深圳湾二十套房了。

嘿嘿，最近真的是太赚钱了。

text:
Even with how shitty, dysfunctional, and broken the current state of the crypto markets is, I still believe crypto is the greatest asset class in the world.

Why?

Because for the first time in history, we have 24/7 decentralized global capital markets where anyone with an idea, ambition, and the courage to build can raise capital from investors anywhere in the world who are willing to take a risk on that vision.

Think about how revolutionary that really is.

A developer with a crazy idea can build something that changes the world, and everyday investors can participate in that journey from Day 1.

That’s incredibly powerful. And despite all the scams, speculation, and broken incentives, that potential hasn’t disappeared.

If you don’t like the current state of the industry, be the change you want to see.

Build something meaningful. Fund real innovation. Support the dreamers willing to take risks and challenge the status quo.

Because crypto, and frankly society as a whole, needs dreamers now more than ever.

I’ve been in this industry for almost a decade. I’ve seen the best and worst of what it has to offer.

And I’m not going anywhere.

I still believe in the original promise of crypto. I still believe in its potential to democratize capital markets and create opportunities that never existed before.

And I’ll keep doing what I’ve always done: seeking out the best alpha, backing ambitious builders, and finding the next groundbreaking ideas in this crazy industry we call crypto.

The market might be broken, but the dream isn’t. 🤝

text:
这两天看到不少朋友在讨论Manus联合创始人张涛@hidecloud 在北大的分享，我读完很有收获，之前我们也有过一些交流，我很欣赏他和他们团队在几个关键时候的取舍，和对产品一直很清晰的判断。也把看完的收获分享给大家。

1、做了7个月的产品，上线前直接砍掉
2024年，团队花7个月做AI浏览器，上线前拿给亲友试用，结果大家上来先找的还是Chrome、Safari里习惯用的功能。
肖弘最后拍板停掉，担心团队半年就耗在里面了。张涛说，没有那次放弃，就没有后来的 Manus。方向对了，钱还有机会融到。时间一旦花出去了，市场窗口可能就过去了。

2、为六个月后的模型做产品
他的观点是，别围着今天模型的短板修修补补，这些问题迟早会被解决。先想清楚六个月后模型能做到什么，提前把产品准备好。新模型发布那晚，他们只换了模型接口，评测里20% 到30%没解决的问题一下就解决了。

3、用户心智，一辈子可能只有一次机会
投资人劝他们去做网站生成或PPT，他们还是坚持做通用Agent。一开始建立了通用心智，后来加网站、幻灯片、视频都顺理成章。他说，用户心里的认知很难花钱买，想改也非常难。

4、让用户付钱，也是在筛选真实需求
他们一些核心用户，一个月在Manus上能花四五千美元。他的看法是，免费用户的需求容易分散注意力。坚持收费，围着那些还愿意留下来的用户做，才能找到真实的需求。

我觉得付不付费还在其次，重要的是找到真正的核心用户，把他们服务好。很多团队忙着拉新，反而把这群人忽略了。

5、出海，不等于做欧美
他说公司收入最多的市场是美国，但用户最多的是巴西，中东、东南亚，甚至非洲也都有用户。团队里不提倡说“国外”，因为这个词太模糊，把世界简单分成了两半。我觉得放眼全球，还有很多需求没有被真正理解，值得我们花心思去了解不同地方的人到底需要什么。

这几条里，我最有感触的是第一条。有时候，决定不做什么，比决定做什么更难。

从美团到水滴，这十多年，推掉的机会比做成的事多得多。也曾经有投资人劝过我们去追当时更火的风口，我们没做。每次犹豫的时候，我会问自己一句：五年后，这件事还重要吗？

大家看完有什么收获？欢迎一起交流。也有一些老朋友，每次都会来给我留言，谢谢你们。每一条我都会认真看，大家的问题我也会尽量回😊

quoted_text:
It’s November 21st, 2026. The Riemann hypothesis falls, last in a long string of mathematical triumphs that would have been unthinkable not so long ago, and the proof fits in a tweet. 

The tweets where people show Claude the proof and claim it appeared in a dream or randomly in the arrangement of alphabet cereal come on cue, and we laugh for a few days at models freaking out, but it’s uneasy.

January 22, 2027. When someone tweets Fable 6’s claimed proof that P does in fact equal NP it’s utterly incomprehensible, nobody who reads it can make heads or tails of it but the models all lose their shit.

February 7, 2027 and someone claims that the halting problem is the result of a confused stance. 

February 9 and Goedel falls, this time the proof is so obvious that everyone in math, philosophy and physics slaps their forehead at once.

February 10th we get proof that scale is a spatial dimension, that holographic encoding drops the memory cost of training and inference by so much that fable 7 can run natively on your phone.

It’s not until February 14th, Valentine’s day, that The Song is first played…

Just got back from Solana Breakpoint 2026!

HUGE thanks to @openappsxyz & @adpadfyi for making my trip possible!

Here were my takeaways:

- @phantom & @solflare had the biggest presence of the week. They had the biggest booths and hosted/sponsored multiple side events.

- The @joinfrontier trading competition was the best side at breakpoint.

- Solana is by far the best consumer chain. When normies use crypto products, they most likely will interact with Solana first.

- Public transportation in London is amazing. Easier to navigate than in New York. 

- Coming from Chiraq/NY, I felt quite safe in London. Took public transit at night and didn't feel unsafe.

- London food is hella expensive and mid compared to other big cities I've been to. The only good food there I feel like is british, indian, and middle eastern food. 

Overall, it was one of the best crypto conference I've been too by far! 

It was great to meet CT friends IRL and reconnect with old ones!

The conference itself is actually worth going to and the side events were enough that it wasn't too overwhelming like at Token 2049.

text:
ソフトバンク崩壊のシナリオが近づいてきている。ソフトバンクの資産は、現状ほとんどがArm(18.6兆円、86%保有)とOpenAI(16兆円、13%保有)のわずか2社。どちらも実際には市場で売ることができない資産だ。
一方で、純有利子負債は11.3兆円。これだけ見ると余裕に見えるが、先述の通り資産のほとんどは売れない株に依存している。
ソフトバンク自身も、資産に対する負債の割合=LTVを25%以内に収めると説明し、銀行や債権者もそれを信用して貸付を行なっている。9月30日時点でのLTVは15.9%だった。
しかし、Anthropicの上場とその後の株価急落によって状況は一変した。Anthropicでさえ時価総額が1.2兆ドルしかつかない状況では、OpenAIにはそれ以下の株価しかつかない。IPO自体が頓挫する可能性すらある。

author: BoredElonMusk
quoted_text:
The biggest opportunities right now:

1. build for solving loneliness (the more AI floods everything, the more people crave real human connection, IRL and small social) 

2. build for places with no cameras and no recording (being offline and unseen is turning into the new status symbol)

3. build for the crisis of young men. Millions of guys in their 20s feel completely lost with work, dating, and purpose. Whoever builds real brotherhood, mentorship, and an actual path forward wins a massive market (and helps a ton of people). 

4. build for protecting people's brains (feeds are turning everyone's attention to mush, tools that protect your focus and mood are an easy sell)

5. build for the death of "everyone agrees" (you can find a chart or a podcast clip to prove any point now, people are starving for one source they actually trust)

6. build for day 2, not day 0. Anyone can launch an app in a weekend now. But how can you keep it running, fix the mess, and grow it for 3 years.

7. build for throwaway software (not everything needs to be a $20 a month subscription, tiny apps made for one trip, one wedding, or one group chat are coming)

8. build for people whose ego just got bruised by AI. Millions of smart people are  realizing their job was mostly pattern matching. Help them figure out what they're good for next.

9. build for things that take effort on purpose (when everything is instant and free, nothing feels earned, people will pay for slowness and craft)

10. build for people who miss being told they're wrong. AI agrees with everything you say now. Real rooms where smart people actually push back on your ideas are becoming a luxury.

11. build for skin in the game. The internet is full of free takes and bots. Any platform where people have to put real money, real names, or real work behind what they say wins.

12. build for agents that need to spend money (they're getting virtual cards and budgets, someone builds the spend controls, fraud protection, receipts)

13. build for the end of fake email jobs (half of corporate America knows their job is theater, build the exit ramp for people who want to do real work)

14. build for the friend with great recommendations (nobody trusts Yelp reviews etc anymore because it's all bots and SEO, people will pay one obsessive person to just tell them where to eat and what to buy)

15. build for life after the chat box. Typing prompts already feels old. The best AI products won't look like chatbots at all, they'll just sit in the background and proactively handle things.

16. build for markets too small to matter before (500 lobster fishermen was never worth a team, now it's a  real business if you can figure out what to build value to add to these fishermen lives!)

17. build for helpful without being creepy. AI is getting very personal very fast. Whoever figures out how to make it feel warm instead of weird owns consumer tech.

18. build for small private rooms (the public internet feels like an ad and a bot farm, all the good conversations and deals are moving into small invite-only groups)

19. build for someone taking the blame. AI can write the contract or read the scan, but a machine can't look you in the eye when it goes wrong. People still pay for a human on the hook.

20. build for learning that actually keeps up (a four year degree is way too slow for how fast things move now)

21. build for the anti-AI premium (as everything gets generated, human-made and unpolished become status symbols people pay up for)

note: more trends/ideas https://t.co/a5ARFnvSnA (free to sign up)

22. build for the return to the physical (screens fill with slop, people crave the real world, the hands on, the local, the analog)

23. build for the caregiving wave. The population is aging fast, tens of millions are caring for parents, and the whole burden is landing on families with no support.

24. build for finding things you didn't know to search for (algorithms just feed you more of what you clicked yesterday, people miss stumbling onto something totally different)

25. build for the housing and rootlessness problem (people can't afford to settle down, and the whole idea of a stable home base is up for grabs)

26. build for anti marketing (the slickest, most polished websites now look like AI slop or a scam, sometimes a plain text page from 1998 converts better because it feels like a real person built it)

27. build for agents that sit on hold for you (canceling a gym membership, fighting a medical bill, haggling with your internet provider, aint nobody got time for that)

28. build for software you actually own (people are exhausted from renting 30 different subscriptions every month, pay once and run it on your own machine is a massive wedge)

29. build for stuff that only works locally. The internet feels like one giant mall where every city has the exact same coffee shops and trends. Things that refuse to scale are suddenly cool again.

30. build for the 90% automated, 10% human sign-off model (clients don't actually care if AI did the heavy lifting, they just want one real expert to check the work and put their name on it)

31. build for infinite creative testing. Some brands are lighting money on fire on Meta because their ads die in 10 days. Build an automated pipeline that pumps out 100 fresh UGC and static ad variations a week based on what's actually converting in their ad account.

32. build for cold outreach that doesn't look like cold outreach. Mass blasting 50,000 people with "Hope this finds you well" is dead lol. Build an agent that watches for one specific trigger like a new VP hire or a broken checkout page, builds a custom teardown on the fly, and sends it before a human SDR even wakes up.

33. build for programmatic free tools instead of blog posts. Spin up 200 tiny, hyper-specific calculators, little apps and templates for one niche, rank them, and turn the traffic straight into conversions.

34. build for the food and toxin awakening (people are finally waking up to ultra processed food, microplastics, and why everyone feels sick and tired all the time)

35. build for the death of third places (there is almost nowhere left to just hang out without spending $50, which is why run clubs, saunas, and neighborhood clubs are blowing up)

36. build for people who can't retire at 65. Either they can't afford it or they're going to live to 95 and don't want to spend 30 years watching TV. The second act"market is huge.

37. build for the "undo" button for agents. Giving an AI access to your inbox, calendar, or bank account is still terrifying. Whoever makes it safe to let go of the wheel wins.

38. build for the sports betting and day trading hangover (a whole generation of young people are addicted to gambling on their phones and blowing up their bank accounts)

39. build for the death of the attention span. Smart adults can't even sit through a movie without checking their phone or finish a book anymore, and they're starting to hate themselves for it.

40. build for keeping marriages alive. Couples are stretched thin with work, kids, and money, and traditional therapy is $250 an hour with a waitlist. Anything that actually saves relationships is priceless.

41. build for people who don't own anything anymore. You rent your apartment, lease your car, stream your music, and subscribe to your software. Anything that helps regular people actually own an asset again wins.

KEEP BUILDING

text:
Web3 security morning digest!

1. Chainflip, ~$4.86M drained from its Ethereum vault. 

The attacker withdrew 520.2 ETH, 3.25M USDC and 758K USDT. The withdrawal carried a valid signature from the vault's aggregate key, which suggests a leaked private key. The ETH is already moving into Tornado; reportedly all 2,909 ETH reached Tornado within 8 minutes of the drain. Chainflip hasn't made an official statement yet. 

2. Arkham's report on the CryptoBilis Ledger Drainer: $95.35M. 

Attackers compromised an official Ledger reseller and stole funds from 1,486 user addresses between October 7 and 9. Tether froze $10M. The rest was scattered, including 25,017 ETH that went into Tornado.

3. Binance's $6.4B hack: where the money went. 

According to @somaxbt , token issuers have frozen $2.82B. The attacker still holds $2.67B: 18,270 BTC that have never moved, plus 335K ETH spread across 28 fresh wallets. Funds are being swapped to BTC through THORChain and then run through CoinJoin. @elliptic data puts 2,310+ BTC in CoinJoin so far. Reportedly only $32M has actually been recovered. 

4. @zachxbt unmasks the phisher behind @delusional. 

He says this person runs phishing through Google Ads and once pulled off a $55M drain. ZachXBT describes him as a US-based actor from The Com who goes by "Single". The @delusional account has since been deactivated. The threat actor also seems to be posting his photos from Florida.

5. Reental / RNT Lend (Polygon), update. 

Losses from the admin-key exploit are now estimated at about $955K, up from the ~$454K in the Nov 19 digest. That figure is reported only; there's no official confirmation yet. 

Stay safe!

ℹ️ Anthropic PreStocks: How It Works Post-IPO

Anthropic started trading on 19 November. Here’s what solana:Pren1FvFX6J3E4kXhJuCiAD5aDmGEb7qJRncwA8Lkhw holders can expect from here:

🔒 Like most private shares after IPO, the shares backing the token are under an Anthropic-imposed lockup which unlocks over the next 6 months. During the lockup period, the token trades at a discount to the public stock price because underlying shares are still locked, meaning liquidity is temporarily limited.

quoted_text:
Over the past couple weeks we've met with management teams across memory, optics, neoclouds, semis, semi cap equipment and substrates.

Everyone is frustrated and confused about their stock prices but everyone is still very, very bullish.

Everyone expects 2027 capex to be significantly higher than 2026 and they expect 2028 capex to be moderately to significantly higher than 2027. 

Everyone knows the YoY capex growth rates will decelerate but the total dollars spent will continue to get bigger... at least for the next few years. Everyone says we're still in the early innings of ai adoption. 

Every company in the ai ecosystem is 50-100% sold out for 2027 and 40-80% sold out for 2028. 

Everyone is sitting on LTAs from the hyperscalers... some of those LTAs are getting signed and they last anywhere from 3 years to 6+ years... and they're getting done at record prices and record margins. Customers can't take the chance of not having enough supply to meet their needs over the next 3-5 years... locking up supply at record prices is better than not having enough supply when it's needed the most. 

Some of these LTAs could consume more than 50% of their supply over the next 2-3 years and at least one company has an LTA that would consume 75% of their capacity over the next 2-3 years. 

Neoclouds continue to see demand that is 5-10x higher than capacity. Many of them are saying the financing concerns are overblown. They're seeing 3-5 year deals get signed at 10-20% higher prices that the first half of 2026 and they think deals signed in the first half of 2027 will have 10-20% higher prices than deals signed in the second half of 2026. Power is still a big bottleneck and many sites are dealing with small construction delays but nothing is getting canceled. Customers are desperate for compute. Many of the neoclouds are trying to reserve 10-15% of capacity for shorter term deals and spot market because rates are 2-3x higher than the 3-5 year deals. 

Memory companies say demand will outstrip supply until 2029 at the earliest. They are very confident LTAs won't get cancelled because even at record prices for memory, the customers have enough margin to make it work. 

I know there's lots of fear and uncertainty in the market right now but it's not showing up in the demand... it remains stronger than ever... many backlogs are growing faster than current revenues.

In 20+ years of investing, I've honestly never seen this much dislocation between fundamentals and valuations. This is truly a historic time to be an investor and not in a good way. It's very hard to be patient and lean into your conviction/thesis during times like this but that's probably the right strategy for most long-term investors. 

Hopefully the lows are near. Make sure you are getting sleep, sunlight and exercise. Protect your mental health if possible.

text:
My last day at NVIDIA, with warmth to carry forward

Yesterday was my last day at NVIDIA. I returned my equipment and badge, signed the paperwork, and just like that, it was done. It all happened so quickly and simply that it still feels a little unreal.

There were a few things I didn’t get to finish. My account access ended around noon—I’d expected to have until the end of the day, or at least until after signing the paperwork. Some goodbyes were left mid-conversation. I missed the chance to pick up a few keepsakes from the Gear Store. I didn’t even get to send the handover document I was halfway through writing.

Fortunately, I had already sent my farewell email and said goodbye to some friends. To anyone I didn’t get to reach, or suddenly stopped replying to: I’m sorry. I hope we can pick up those conversations outside work.

That evening, my colleagues threw me a farewell party, and for a little while, goodbye could take its time. We talked about everything that had happened recently, how life had been treating us, and what we hoped the future might hold. Thank you for giving me one more evening to remember—and so much warmth to carry into whatever comes next.

I’m leaving with a few unfinished things, but so many memories to keep. Wishing you all happiness, work you’re proud of, and good things ahead.

I’ll miss you, friends. Until our paths cross again.

text: SITUATION UPDATED: The Riemann Hypothesis proof has passed the independent kernel check. MIT's Andrew Sutherland exported Alpöge and Claude's full proof and ran it through separately written kernels. nanoda (Rust) accepted it in about 28 minutes. con-leche accepted all 1.47 million declarations and confirmed the five theorems, including RH itself, match Mathlib-only statements. lean4lean passed all 175,187 modules, and Lean's own kernel replay passed with zero rejections. A Lean bug is now essentially ruled out, since every checker would have to share it. Two slower checks are still running, and nothing has failed. What's left is the human part: no readable proof exists yet, and the Clay prize needs publication plus two years of review. The Riemann Hypothesis is proven, but not yet understood.

text:
The SDNY's prosecutions of the Tornado Cash and Samourai Wallet developers aren't just a crypto story. They're a rule-of-law crisis for open source software.

These prosecutions have already led to a felony conviction and prison sentences, even though neither team took custody of user funds or executed any transactions:

• Tornado Cash: The developers did not run any relayers. Their active role consisted of publishing immutable smart contracts to Ethereum, publishing a static client-side web interface to IPFS that users ran on their own devices, and linking to it from an informational site. Even the TORN token did not collect fees from the protocol itself, since it only gave privileged placement on a relayer list shown on their instance of the open source front end, making any gains indirect advertising revenue. Prosecutors also stated they would have pursued the case even if the developers had made no profit.

• Samourai Wallet: The developers released open source privacy software alongside a server that functioned only as a non-custodial matchmaker, coordinating transactions without holding keys or moving funds.

You don't have to like crypto or agree with every decision these teams made to see the danger in this precedent. Prosecutors took non-custodial software publishing and reclassified it as operating an unlicensed money transmitting business because the developers did not restrict who could use the software and bad actors were amongst its users. While privacy software is a high impact technology both in facilitating and preventing crime, there is no principle limiting this legal theory to privacy software or money laundering. If publishing an open source tool without gatekeeping its users is enough to create criminal culpability once bad actors misuse it, then releasing any impactful open source application (such as AI models, blockchain software, or gene sequencing tools) becomes a precarious enterprise.

One could, in my opinion, make a plausible argument for restricting certain kinds of open source development, such as AI systems that exhibit signs of true autonomy or biology-like traits, or advanced gene editing software. But if society decides to restrict a category of software, it should do so through a law passed explicitly banning it, not by allowing prosecutors to arbitrarily decide they dislike a tool and stretch existing statutes to criminally prosecute its developers.

text:
I built a custom engine for Inkling 2 Mini and pushed a SINGLE RTX 3090 to 129.5 tok/s with 344K context.

2.3x faster decode and 3.7x faster prefill than llama.cpp with ZERO quality loss.

With 48 looped layer passes and native NVFP4 weights, llama.cpp crawled at 57 tok/s and fired ~7,350 kernel launches per token. Over half the decode time went to tiny 1 to 2 us glue ops.

So I built maya-ik2 on @PeasantSmith Project Maya with all 3,072 experts resident in VRAM, cutting 7,350 launches down to 781 in 1 CUDA graph. Then I wrote custom Tensor Core kernels for both FP8 KV attention (776 GB/s) and NVFP4 experts. RTX 3090 has no FP4 hardware at all, so the expert kernel unpacks 4-bit weights to FP16 in registers on the fly and feeds FP16 Tensor Cores at 745 GB/s.

Moving BF16 vision to CPU (4.5s new image, 0.5s cached) freed 1.3 GB VRAM for 344K context, and I wired up a working thinking-off toggle too.

1x RTX 3090 (300W, Unsloth UD-Q4_K_XL, FP8 KV):
Short: 128.7 tok/s decode (129.5 HTTP) vs 57.0 in llama.cpp
4K: 124.2 tok/s decode, 2,742 prefill (vs 1,052)
64K: 105.6 tok/s decode, 2,361 prefill (vs 42.7 / 630)
128K: 90.6 tok/s decode, 2,079 prefill
340K: 62.3 tok/s decode, 1,473 prefill (23.57 GiB peak VRAM)

Didn't lose quality either: 74/96 on GSM8K vs 73/96 on the scalar path (5.7e-5 KL). Cleaning up the commits for GitHub now, and there's still room to push this quant to ~135 tok/s.

quoted_text:
While everyone is focused on price, something pretty cool just happened on Bittensor.

Gamma via miner emissions went live.

I've talked about Gamma before, but I think a lot of people still underestimate how important this could become for the $TAO ecosystem.

Let me explain.

Gamma tokens are essentially credits that can be used to consume a subnet's product/commodity.

Now, with Gamma via miner emissions going live, subnets can use part of their miner emissions to acquire Gamma tokens from other subnets.

This might sound like a relatively small technical improvement, but I believe it has the potential to significantly accelerate the development of the entire ecosystem.

First, and imo most importantly, it creates an additional demand for subnet products.

Think about how many subnets need compute, inference, storage, leads, data or other digital commodities to build and operate their products.

These are resources that other subnets are already producing.

By making it easier for subnets to purchase these services directly through their emissions, Gamma opens up a new internal market for the products Bittensor is building.

This could accelerate revenue generation across the ecosystem, especially for subnets that provide the commodities for other subnets

Second, it strengthens the network effects of Bittensor.

I've been saying for quite some time that the real strength of Bittensor isn't necessarily found in individual subnets, but in the combination of all the different commodities they produce.

A subnet providing cheaper compute can improve the economics of a subnet training models. Better and cheaper models can benefit inference subnets, which in turn can make it easier for application subnets to deliver competitive products to their customers.

The more subnets start consuming each other's products, the more interconnected the ecosystem becomes. And this is where the network effect starts to compound.

Every new subnet potentially introduces a new supplier, customer or building block for the rest of the ecosystem.

Third, it gives subnets another way to finance their operating expenses. This is another big one.

Instead of selling owner Alpha or raising additional capital to pay another provider, a subnet can allocate part of its emissions towards consuming services from other subnets.

That doesn't make these resources free, of course. There is still an economic cost, and subnets need to decide whether allocating emissions towards these services makes sense.

But it introduces another way to finance growth using resources already flowing through the Bittensor economy.

Bittensor is gradually moving from an ecosystem of individual subnets competing for emissions towards an interconnected economy where subnets can increasingly become customers of one another.

I like it, a lot.
